results.summary: I checked about 50 sources online. The verification log, with URLs and what each check confirmed, is teams/prior/citations-log.md; UNVERIFIED items are marked there and nothing relies on them. In literature terms the model is a multiphase minimal partition with an air reservoir: same material means zero tension, so one phase; different materials meet across a film of tension g; equilibria obey Plateau's laws (Plateau 1873, Taylor 1976, Morgan 1994). The engine reproduces the Young/Neumann closed form for a 2D double bubble: wall within 0.004 blocks and tip within 0.021 blocks at n=64, for g = 0.5, 1 and 1.5. A block lattice is almost never a Plateau configuration. Of 738 corner classes, only 85 pass Plateau's necessary checks and 650 have a four-film lattice line, so on blocks bubble physics is first a set of T1/pop decisions. The lower-tension diagonal wins; ties are common, and the owner's painted diagonal line is a chain of ties that physics does not decide. The persistent four-way junction in the README has an exact cause: with equal tensions the Gaussian-thresholded axis-aligned cross is a fixed point (0 changes within 1 block over 5 steps), and a T1 nucleus of 2 sub-cells or less collapses back. The engine's jitter is frozen per cell, phase and seed. Re-drawing it every step (auction dynamics' 'temperature', Jacobs et al. 2018) at 0.1 for 100 steps, then quenching, resolved the junction in 5/5 2D and 3/3 3D runs; frozen or 1e-2 noise never did. Pinning (Esedoglu-Ruuth-Tsai; Misiats-Yip 2016) is real but narrower than the README's half-sub-cell rule: plain-MBO disks shrink at the theoretical rate up to R=2 at n=16 and R=6 at n=32. The FID regime is TV-L1 (Chan-Esedoglu 2005): without volume the corner radius follows r = s/(k*sqrt(2*pi)) at 82-95 %, but with volume rounding nearly vanishes and k=0.15 oscillates. Volume preservation makes the model non-local (106 cells differ 4 blocks from an edit after 6 steps, 0 without volume). Seam grooves are Mullins thermal grooves with opening angle 2*acos(g/2). REPORT.md was NOT written: the harness refused report files from subagents, so the full report content is in this structured result. Everything else is in teams/prior/ and was backed up with rsync.

claims.statement: A 2x2x2 lattice corner has 21,147 equality patterns (materials compared only for equality; air distinguished), falling into 738 classes under the 48 cube symmetries. Only 85 classes pass Plateau's two necessary checks: no lattice line with four films around it, and at most 4 regions meeting at the point. 650 classes contain a four-film line and 280 have more than 4 regions. Restricted to surface corners with at most 2 solid materials: 132 classes, 92 with a four-film line, 49 of them with a tension tie. Binary solid/air (today's mesher): 20 classes; 9 have a four-film line, all ties, and these are PLAN 7.2's pinched diagonal-only contacts. Under bubble physics most corners therefore need a topological decision (T1/pop, as in the Surface Evolver's 'O'/'o'/'pop' commands) before any smoothing.
claims.numbers: 738 classes / 21147 labelled; 85 Plateau-passing; 650 with X-line; 280 >4 regions; surface<=2 solids 132/92/49; binary 20 classes, 9 with X-line; orchestrator cross-check 738/551/22
claims.refuteBy: Enumerate independently and get different counts. Or anneal and quench a configuration (several seeds) and show that a four-film line, or a point where more than 4 regions meet, survives as a stable equilibrium.

claims.statement: A four-way (X) junction on a lattice edge with unit outer films at 90 degrees, split by a central film of tension tau and length L, changes energy by (tau - sqrt2)*L to first order. The outer-film term is the same for both splits, so the diagonal pair with the lower film tension gets the central film. Engine tensions: same material 0 (unites), air-air 0, solid-air 1, solid-solid g. Decided cases: ABAC and ABA-air (the A pair unites), air-A-air-B (A and B stay apart). Ties: ABAB (checkerboard), A-air-A-air (diagonal-only contact), ABCD, plus ABC-air at the default g=1. The decision lives on the 4 blocks around one lattice edge: 52 labelled patterns, 17 classes, 7 with an X, 3 tied at generic g and 4 at g=1. The owner's painted 1-wide diagonal line of A in B is a chain of AB/BA ties, so physics does not decide whether it connects; a tie policy must (cf. the asymptotic decider, Nielson-Hamann 1991; (8,4) connectivity, Kong-Rosenfeld 1989).
claims.numbers: dE = (tau - 1.414) L; per-edge table 52 patterns / 17 classes / 7 X / 3 ties (4 at g=1)
claims.refuteBy: Run 2D FREE on ABA-air or ABAC 2x2 configurations with annealed noise 0.1 and a quench, over 10 seeds. If the higher-tension diagonal (B-air or B-C) gets the central wall in most seeds, the rule is wrong.

claims.statement: With equal tensions among the four phases, the axis-aligned four-phase cross is an exact fixed point of the engine's Gaussian threshold step. The blurred quadrant indicators are products Phi(x/s)Phi(y/s), so each cell's lowest cost is its own quadrant. This is the cause of README limit 2 (a persistent X), rather than generic pinning. No paper found states this for threshold dynamics; the derivation is this team's.
claims.numbers: 0 label changes within 1 block of the cross over 5 steps, for g=1 and g=0.5, with and without the volume solve (n=32, four 2x2-block quadrants)
claims.refuteBy: With jitter 0 and equal tensions, find any label change within 1 block of an axis-aligned four-phase cross.

claims.statement: In 2D sq2-ABCD FREE (n=32, s=6.4 sub-cells, jitter 0), a seeded A-D T1 nucleus of radius 1 or 2 sub-cells collapses back to the X. Radius 3 to 16 survives, but the final wall freezes at a length that depends on the seed instead of reaching one equilibrium. So the X is stable at sub-kernel scale, and walls are pinned once formed.
claims.numbers: r=1,2: X restored; r=3,4,6,8,12,16: final A-D contact 2,6,12,12,14,16 face-adjacent sub-cell pairs
claims.refuteBy: Rerun xjunc.mjs presplit. A wall surviving at r<=2, or final wall lengths that do not depend on r (one equilibrium), refutes it.

claims.statement: The engine's jitter is a frozen function of (cell, phase, seed). Re-drawing it every step, as in auction dynamics' temperature (Jacobs-Merkurjev-Esedoglu 2018, sec. 3.4), at amplitude 0.1 for 100 steps followed by a jitter-0 quench resolves the four-material X in 2D and the four-film line in 3D. Frozen noise at 1e-3 or 1e-2, and re-drawn noise at 1e-2, do not.
claims.numbers: 2D: frozen 1e-3 and 1e-2 X persists 6/6; annealed 1e-2 3/3 persist; anneal 0.03 x100 + quench 1/5 resolved; anneal 0.1 x100 + quench 5/5 resolved (1 A-D, 4 B-C). 3D (n=16): persists at jitter 0, frozen 1e-3, annealed 1e-2; anneal 0.1 + quench 3/3 resolved (seed 2 one B-C wall 0.719 blocks^2; seeds 1 and 3 both walls ~0.74-0.80 blocks^2)
claims.refuteBy: Run anneal 0.1 + quench on seeds 6-20. Persisting Xs in more than a few seeds refute it. So does frozen jitter of amplitude 0.1 resolving the X equally often, which would show that re-drawing is not what matters.

claims.statement: For the 2D equal double bubble with A-B tension g, the engine (FREE, measured on labels) matches the Young/Neumann closed form: R^2[pi - acos(g/2) + (g/2)sqrt(1-g^2/4)] = 1, wall half-length R*sqrt(1-g^2/4), wall-to-tip R(1+g/2).
claims.refuteBy: Rerun at n=128. Diverging from the closed form refutes it, as does an independent solver (e.g. Surface Evolver string model) giving different junction geometry for g=0.5.

claims.statement: Where an A-B wall meets air, Young's balance (Mullins 1957, thermal grooving) sets the opening angle of the air surface at 2*acos(g/2): 120 deg at g=1, 151 deg at g=0.5, 83 deg at g=1.5. So the grooves at different-material seams in the orchestrator's FID images are the expected geometry, not an artefact. A small g (<=0.25 gives >=166 deg) nearly removes the groove, but the same tension is what straightens a jagged seam, so smoothness of boundaries trades off against seam flatness (inference).
claims.numbers: opening 151.0 / 120 / 82.8 deg (theory, results-neumann.json); junction geometry matched at n=64 (claim young-neumann-engine)
claims.refuteBy: Measure the groove angle on labels in 3D FID seam runs at g in {0.25, 1, 1.5}. An angle that does not depend on g, or does not follow 2acos(g/2) within the resolution, refutes it.

claims.statement: The FID-k regime is the TV-L1 / flat-norm problem min Per + lambda*|symmetric difference| (Chan-Esedoglu 2005). From the engine's costs a boundary cell keeps its phase while |kappa| <= k*sqrt(2*pi)/s, so convex block corners round to r = s/(k*sqrt(2*pi)), with s in blocks and kappa the sum of principal curvatures in 3D. Without the volume solve this holds at 82-95 %. With the volume solve on (the study's FID regime) corners barely round, and k=0.15 never converges (a 2-cycle).
claims.refuteBy: Change s at fixed k without the volume solve; r not scaling linearly with s refutes it. Showing that the volume-on 2-cycle disappears with an exact (auction) volume solve would make that part a solver artefact, not inherent.

claims.statement: Plain MBO (no volume, s=0.2 blocks) shrinks disks at the curve-shortening rate pi*s^2 = 0.126 blocks^2/step up to R=2 blocks at n=16 and R=6 at n=32. At n=16 it slows from R=2.25 and freezes at R=3-4. The half-sub-cell estimate R_pin ~ s^2*n (0.64 / 1.28 blocks) is at least 3.5x too pessimistic for curved boundaries. Inference: pinning in the study mostly comes from grid-aligned flats (block faces) and from volume-constrained runs near equilibrium, where the driving force is only a curvature difference. Literature: MBO 'gets stuck' (Esedoglu-Ruuth-Tsai citing MBO 1994); orientation-dependent pinning regimes (Misiats-Yip 2016).
claims.refuteBy: Repeat with disk centres at random sub-cell offsets. Pinning at R<=1.28 for n=32 refutes the measured part. An axis-aligned flat with small imposed curvature that moves freely refutes the inference.

claims.statement: Without volume the engine has a hard reach of ceil(3s) = 20 sub-cells = 0.625 blocks per step (n=32 2D, n=16 3D). With volume, each bubble's pressure lambda is global (Young-Laplace), so an edit changes the shape far away. Inference for amorfus: apron 3 can host NOVOL-T for T<=4; volume-preserving regimes need the per-cluster pressure computed outside the chunk job.
claims.numbers: A bar grown from 6 to 10 blocks, labels compared at x<2 (4 blocks away): NOVOL-6 0 differing cells, FINITE-6 (volume) 106 of 9216, FID-0.15 0 (not converged in 200 steps), FID-0.15 without volume 0
claims.refuteBy: Find NOVOL-T differences beyond T*0.625 blocks. Or find volume-on FINITE runs with zero differences at the same distance across several geometries, which would mean the lambda coupling is negligible in practice.

claims.statement: The engine's tension matrix (solid-air 1, different materials g, same material separate clusters 0.05) is conditionally negative semi-definite in every tested phase set for g <= 2. That puts it inside Esedoglu-Otto's Proposition 1 class: each step dissipates the nonlocal energy, given a kernel with G >= 0 and Fourier transform >= 0. For g > 2 the triangle inequality fails, because an air film is cheaper than an A-B wall (dewetting); at g=2.5 with 22 phases the matrix also leaves the stability class.
claims.numbers: g in {0.1,...,2}, 3-22 phases: max projected eigenvalue <= 0; g=2.5: triangle slack -0.5, max eigenvalue +0.141 with 7 materials x 3 clusters
claims.refuteBy: Find a phase set with g <= 2 and eps 0.05 whose largest eigenvalue on sum-zero vectors is positive.

claims.statement: A separable tent kernel (box*box, two running sums per axis) satisfies Esedoglu-Otto's kernel conditions (G >= 0, Fourier transform sinc^2 >= 0). It blurs about 2x faster than the engine's truncated Gaussian at the same scale. It is anisotropic, and the gain for a whole step was not measured.
claims.numbers: 96^3 = 884,736 cells, s=3.2 sub-cells: Gaussian 21 taps median 122.2 ms vs tent (box 7, variance 8) median 59.5 ms, speed-up 2.05 (runs 86-206 vs 42-92 ms; noisy)
claims.refuteBy: Repeat the benchmark with a variance-matched tent (box 9) and whole-step timing. A speed-up below 1.2x refutes the optimization's value.

claims.statement: At g=1 with one cluster per material, the engine's costs reduce to psi_i = 1 - u_i for solids and Sall = 1 - u_air for air. One unconstrained threshold step is then exactly the argmax of the per-material Gaussian-blurred block indicators, air included. That is a multi-material blobby/convolution surface (Blinn 1982; Bloomenthal-Shoemake 1991) with selective blending by group (Kacic-Alesic and Wyvill 1991, citing Beier 1990): same material blends (unites), different materials do not. At s=0.2 blocks a lone block keeps about 0.96 of its centre density, so it survives, unlike PLAN 7.7's rejected wide blur.
claims.numbers: psi_i = (1-Sall) + g(Sall - sm) + eps(sm - u_i) = 1 - u_i at g=1, sm=u_i; lone-block centre u ~ erf(0.5/(0.2*sqrt2))^3 ~ 0.96
claims.refuteBy: Run one engine step (volume false, g=1, one cluster per material) and find a cell whose new label differs from the argmax of the blurred indicators including air.

claims.statement: Power-diagram foam models (Busaryev-Dey-Wang-Ren 2012) place walls on radical planes between weighted sites. With one site per block and equal weights (unit volumes) the power diagram is the Voronoi diagram of the lattice, i.e. the block faces themselves, so it adds no smoothing of material walls. It helps only at cluster level, for FREE-like spheres.
claims.refuteBy: Show a per-block weighting that respects the blocks' unit volumes and yields walls that are not lattice planes.

optimizations.idea: Decide T1s per lattice edge with a small table over the equality pattern of the 4 blocks around the edge (52 patterns, 17 classes, 7 with an X). Give the central film to the lower-tension diagonal, break ties with an explicit policy (e.g. connect the locally minority material so painted lines stay whole; that is the owner's call), and check corners only for more than 4 regions. Keep geometry separate from this topology step.
basis: Hege et al. 1997 ZIB SC-97-05 and Wu & Sullivan 2003 IJNME 58 (multi-material MC)
this team's corner-classes.json and the (tau - sqrt2)L derivation
optimizations.gain: Replaces the random noise the engine needs to escape X junctions with a deterministic, local, integer decision that fits the golden-hash rule. The table is tiny (52 entries per edge; 21,147 / 738 classes if indexed per corner).
optimizations.risks: The tie policy is taste, not physics. Decisions on the edges of one corner must be mutually consistent. A tie-break that favours thin painted lines may fill dither and checker patterns.

optimizations.idea: Junction-line fairing as in Frisken 2022: vertices on lines where three or more phases meet (the A|B|air seams on the surface) are smoothed along the line only, other vertices over the surface, all inside a cell-bounded range (the repo's 7.4 constraint box).
basis: Frisken 2022 JCGT 11(1) (EdgeVertex vs SurfaceVertex fairing, AllowedRange)
Plateau-border / triple-line straightening by wall tension (Young; Mullins 1957)
optimizations.gain: Straight, smooth material seams on the surface at surface-nets cost, local and deterministic: the closest existing algorithm to 'smoothness of boundaries'.
optimizations.risks: Does not decide X junctions (needs the per-edge table). Frisken uses one vertex per cell, while amorfus splits vertices per (corner, material), so it must be adapted. Painted lines still need the tie policy.

optimizations.idea: Set the FID strength from the TV-L1 scale law: without volume, convex corners round to r = s/(k*sqrt(2*pi)); features below radius 2/lambda_eff (lambda_eff = k*sqrt(2*pi)/s) vanish in the global minimizer.
basis: Chan & Esedoglu 2005 SIAM J. Appl. Math. 65 (TV-L1 geometry, disk threshold 2/r)
optimizations.gain: Pick k for a target rounding radius and predict which features disappear, without parameter sweeps.
optimizations.risks: The volume solve breaks the law (rounding suppressed; k=0.15 oscillates). Without volume a lone block may vanish at k=0.15 (inferred, not run). 3D corners follow sum-of-curvatures, so a sphere corner rounds twice as wide as a cylinder edge.

optimizations.idea: Replace the truncated Gaussian blur by a separable tent kernel (box*box via running sums), or design the anisotropy deliberately to keep a blocky-but-soft look.
basis: Esedoglu & Otto 2015 CPAM 68, condition (49): G >= 0 and Fourier transform >= 0
Esedoglu, Jacobs & Zhang 2017 JCP (kernel to anisotropic tension)
optimizations.gain: Measured 2.05x faster blur at s=3.2 on 885k cells (blur only); compact support by construction.
optimizations.risks: Anisotropic surface tension changes the look. Whole-step speed-up not measured; the volume solve and assignment may dominate. Timings were noisy.

optimizations.idea: Budget locality explicitly: NOVOL-T reaches T*0.625 blocks, so T<=4 fits the 3-block apron. Volume-preserving regimes need a global per-cluster pressure computed outside the chunk mesh job.
optimizations.gain: Seam-safe chunk meshing with a known apron.
optimizations.risks: NOVOL is mean-curvature flow: small features shrink and vanish (PLAN 7.4 guards apply). Computing a global pressure per cluster does not fit the current per-chunk job model.

optimizations.idea: In the research engine only: re-draw the jitter every step (temperature), then quench, to escape symmetric X junctions and local minima.
basis: Jacobs, Merkurjev & Esedoglu 2018 JCP 354, sec. 3.4 (temperature; Weaire-Phelan from a shifted cubic lattice)
optimizations.gain: X resolved in 5/5 (2D) and 3/3 (3D) runs, where frozen noise failed in 6/6.
optimizations.risks: Random, so not for the game. Results vary with seed (A-D vs B-C wall; one wall vs both).

optimizations.idea: Use a sub-cell representation in the research engine (signed distance, or area fractions interpolated from psi - lambda) to remove pinning from study results.
basis: Jacobs et al. 2018 sec. 4 sub-pixel trick
optimizations.gain: Equilibrium shapes that do not depend on the seed (fixes the frozen T1 wall lengths and part of the Neumann error at n=32).
optimizations.risks: Improves the research, not the game. Signed-distance variants need redistancing every step.

optimizations.idea: Power-diagram walls (radical planes) for bubble walls.
optimizations.gain: Closed-form walls for cluster-level spheres (FREE-like scenes only).
optimizations.risks: With equal block weights the power diagram is the block grid, so no smoothing of material walls. Low value for amorfus.

openQuestions: Tie policy for A B / B A lattice edges (the owner's painted diagonal line): should the line or the background connect? Physics does not decide; prior art offers only conventions ((8,4) connectivity, the asymptotic decider).
Should volume conservation be part of any game rule at all? It makes the model non-local (106 cells changed 4 blocks from an edit) and suppresses or destabilises FID rounding.

Is the FID + volume 2-cycle (k=0.15, 336/680 cells flipping every step) an artefact of the engine's Jacobi quantile volume solve or inherent? Test with an exact auction-dynamics volume solve on the same 4x4 square.
In 3D sq2-ABCD, which has lower energy: the pairwise-touching (tetrahedral-cone) cluster of seeds 1 and 3, or the single wall of seed 2? A Surface Evolver run would settle it.
How strong is pinning on grid-aligned flat faces and on volume-constrained shapes near equilibrium, which the disk test does not cover?
What A-B tension g gives the preferred balance between seam groove depth (opening angle 2acos(g/2)) and seam straightening? This needs a 3D seam test across g under FID.

results.summary:
I tested lib/mbo.mjs (FREE regime) three ways: against closed-form bubble geometry (exact.mjs), against an independent 2D foam solver I wrote (foam2d.mjs), and over the whole catalogue plus 8 extra configurations, with jitter 1e-3 and seeds 1 and 2. The solver uses polyline films, Lagrange-multiplier area constraints and T1 splits. Against the closed forms it reaches 2e-4 relative energy at h 0.04 and 5e-5 at h 0.02, junction angles of 120 ± 0.09°, and pressures within 0.03 % (cross2d/solvercheck.json).

The engine is trustworthy for single bubbles and small clusters:
- Sphere radii are within 0.2 %, and its pressure follows Young–Laplace, λ = (2/R)·s_b/√(2π), to 1–3 %.
- Two-cluster results match the exact double bubble to a few percent.
- 2D interfaces converge to the exact films (mean 0.002 blocks at n 128).
- Bubble–bubble–bubble junctions measure 120.0 ± 0.6°.

It is not trustworthy in five places:
- **Blur width:** its limit at fixed blur s is a slightly different model. The junction circle is +6 % at n 32 and s 0.2, and +10–12 % at s 0.3. Junctions involving air are too wide: about +9° at s 0.2 and about +20° at s 0.3.
- **Pinning:** it stalls whenever a bubble's radius exceeds R_pin = 2·s_b²·n (1.28 blocks at the default n 16, about 9 blocks of volume). Large clusters stay as rounded boxes, and walls with a radius above R_pin stay flat on lattice planes.
- **Exact ties:** it keeps unstable four-fold junctions, always for four materials and for a symmetric checkerboard without jitter.
- **Merges:** a merged phase can split into disconnected parts that share one pressure.
- **Contact rule:** for two materials touching along an edge it adheres at s 0.2 and separates at s 0.1.

On the physics:
- Lattice four-fold junctions always split at once, and the diagonal pair with the higher pressure (the smaller cluster; air counts as 0) becomes connected. The engine follows this in every unequal case: 16 of 16 runs in 2D and 4 of 4 in 3D.
- This local rule can pick a higher-energy end state than the global minimum: 12.916 against 12.243 in checker-smallA.
- Chains of three bubbles have a neutral bending mode.

With these corrections, pattern (a) holds: cluster graph plus volumes decides, once lattice junctions are resolved by the pressure rule, up to that bending mode and exact ties. Pattern (b) holds except at engine-pinned exact ties. Pattern (c) holds: sphere, double-bubble and triple-bubble formulas predict the small results without simulating.

The deliverable REPORT.md was not written: the harness refused writing a report .md file, so the full report is carried in this result. All data, scripts and images are in teams/phys/, backed up to <backup>/teams/phys/.

Method notes:
- lib/ was not edited.
- One heavy node process ran at a time, with --max-old-space-size=700.
- Grids stayed at or below 1.15 M cells. Three big scenes ran at n 12: ball-r2, ball-AB and terrain-step.
- 361 raw renders were deleted to keep 22 images; the scripts regenerate them with fixed seeds.

claims.statement: Single bubbles are right: the radius fitted to the final labels of a 1-, 2- and 8-block FREE bubble is within 0.2% of (3V/4π)^(1/3) at every tested setting with s_b ≥ 0.2 (n 12–32). The engine's pressure (volume multiplier λ during the run) obeys Young–Laplace in engine units, λ = (2/R)·s_b/√(2π), to within 1% for V ≤ 3 and 3.2% for V ≤ 8.
claims.numbers: V1 at n16: R fit 0.6205 vs 0.6204, λ 0.2575 vs 0.2572. V8 at n32: R 1.2411 vs 1.2407. Catalogue λ errors: single −0.9%, pair-same +0.6%, line3 −0.3%, sq2-same +2.4%, plus5 +3.2%, cube2 +1.2%, ring8 −0.5%.
claims.refuteBy: A FREE bubble with V ≤ 8, s_b ≥ 0.2 and n ≥ 12 whose fitted radius is off by more than 1%, or whose λ is off by more than 5% from (2/R)·s_b/√(2π).

claims.statement: At fixed blur the engine converges to a slightly wrong model, not to exact physics. Holding s_b = 0.2 and raising n, the equal double bubble's junction circle moves further from the exact value (+3.0% at n16, +6.4% at n32). At s_b = 0.3 it is +10–12%. Away from junctions the 2D shapes do converge to the exact films.
claims.refuteBy: An n ≥ 48 FREE pair-diff run at s_b 0.2 whose label-measured junction radius is within 2% of 0.5685.

claims.statement: Junction angles are right where three bubbles meet (120.0 ± 0.6°). Where air is one of the three phases, the engine's air sector is too wide, and the excess grows with the blur: about +9° at s_b 0.2, +20° at s_b 0.3 and +3° at s_b 0.1, judged against the same tool applied to the rasterised exact solution. The distortion is confined to a zone of about s around the junction.
claims.numbers: 3D L3-ABC A|B|C junction at n32: 119.97 / 120.62 / 119.41°. 2D pair-diff air sector: 128° (n128, s.2) against an exact-raster reading of 117.9°; 130° (n64, s.3) against 110.0°; 121° (n128, s.1) against 117.9°. 3D fitted-sphere air sector: 117–125° at s.2, 129–133° at s.3. At n ≤ 32 the measuring tool is biased −8 to −25° on air sectors.
claims.refuteBy: An n128 s_b 0.2 2D engine run whose air sector, measured with labtools.anglesAt (rOut 0.35), is within ±3° of the calibrated exact reading of 117.9°.

claims.statement: Where four bubbles meet at a point, the engine forms isolated tetrahedral vertices as Plateau requires. L3-ABC becomes the standard triple bubble with exactly two compact 4-phase points. The 109.47° angle is consistent only on average and is not resolved at affordable n.
claims.refuteBy: A higher-resolution measurement (n ≥ 48, cropped box, or a 3D surface solver) whose mean differs from 109.47° by more than 5°, or one showing a 4-phase line instead of points.

claims.statement: Pinning law: one MBO step moves an interface by about κ·s²/2 and stalls below a sub-cell of motion. A flat face therefore advances only if 2/R > 1/(s_b²·n). Bubbles with R > R_pin = 2·s_b²·n blocks (2D: s_b²·n) end as rounded boxes and are reported as converged. At default settings (n16, s 0.2) R_pin is 1.28, roughly 9 blocks of volume. Walls whose exact radius exceeds R_pin stay exactly planar on a lattice plane.
claims.numbers: Radial spread/R: runs with R/R_pin ≥ 1.45 give 0.20–0.31 (cube3 n16 s.2 0.203; cube4 0.241; n12 s.2 0.267 / 0.307). Runs with R/R_pin ≤ 0.97 give 0.03–0.07 (cube4 n16 s.3 0.030; cube3 n24 s.2 0.053). Runs at 1.15–1.29 give 0.089–0.094. Catalogue: tunnel V30 λ +43.6%, stairs V12 λ +5.9%. The 1:2 wall (exact radius 3.99 > 2.56) has plane rms 0 at n12–32. 2D slab-line at n32: mean / max 0.56/1.24 blocks from equilibrium, energy +7.0%.
claims.refuteBy: A FREE cube with R/R_pin ≥ 1.45 that reaches radial spread < 0.10, or one with R/R_pin ≤ 0.95 that stalls with spread > 0.15.

claims.statement: Lattice four-fold junctions (a 2D corner or a 3D edge with four regions) are never equilibria. They split immediately, and the diagonal pair with the higher pressure (the smaller cluster; air counts as 0) becomes connected. This covers: same material across an air diagonal unites (diag-edge); three bubbles around air form a film between the corner-touching pair (L3-ABC); the slab-line A's unite into a band; the single-block pair unites in unequal checkerboards, whatever its material. The engine agrees whenever the pressures differ.
claims.numbers: The solver's split decision comes one step after the hold, e.g. slab-line A-A rate 1.4174 against B-B 1.4110; L3-ABC B|C 0.4171 against A|air 0.4113. The engine picks the same pair in checker-smallA and checker-smallB: 16 of 16 2D runs (n32 and n64, jitter 0 and 1e-3) and 4 of 4 3D runs. Also diag-edge 10/10, L3-ABC 10/10, and slab-line 2D 5/5 and 3D 2/2 (A band). Exact-film distance at n64 for checker-smallA: 0.011/0.028.
claims.refuteBy: Any exact-solver or engine run without an exact pressure tie in which the lower-pressure diagonal pair of a lattice four-fold junction becomes connected.

claims.statement: At exact pressure ties the engine keeps the non-physical four-fold junction. sq2-checker with jitter 0 keeps its X at every n (32–128) and s_b (0.1–0.2). sq2-ABCD keeps it at every n and jitter tried, sitting on the unstable X-constrained stationary state. The true minimum has a film about 0.46 blocks long between one diagonal pair and different pressures. In 3D the X persists as a 4-fold line.
claims.numbers: sq2-ABCD solver energies: split 11.1884, X kept 11.2916 (+0.92%). Engine distance to the X state: 0.0022/0.0106 (n64), 0.0018/0.0125 (n128). Distance to the true minimum: 0.067/0.143. Engine pressures are uniform at 1.400 (n128); exact are 1.441 (B, C) and 1.357 (A, D). In 3D the 4-fold line has extent 1.25 blocks (both seeds), plus sq2-checker seed 1 at 1.375. With jitter 1e-3 the 2D checker unites one pair: A in 2 of 3 runs at n32, then B and A at n64, B at n128.
claims.refuteBy: An engine FREE run of sq2-ABCD (any n, jitter ≤ 1e-2) that ends with a film between a diagonal pair, or a jitter-0 sq2-checker run that unites a pair.

claims.statement: Uniting is decided locally by pressures at lattice junctions, not by the global energy. In checker-smallA, physics and the engine both unite the single-block pair, giving energy 12.916, although uniting the two 2-block clusters would give 12.243. A 'minimise energy over cluster graphs' predictor would therefore be wrong.
claims.numbers: checker-smallA: rule outcome E 12.9158, forced B-union E 12.2433 (5.2% lower). In slab-line the rule outcome is also the lower one: 31.5168 against 39.5767.
claims.refuteBy: A time-dependent run (solver or engine at n ≥ 64) without an exact tie that reaches the B4 state from the checker-smallA blocks.

claims.statement: The engine has two merge artefacts. (1) A merged phase can come apart into disconnected parts that share one volume and pressure, and is still counted as one united bubble. (2) Sub-cell noise can unite both diagonal pairs of a 2D checkerboard in a single step, which is impossible in a plane.
claims.numbers: sq2-checker 3D seed 1 merged at steps 24 and 27 and ended with both phases in 2 parts, a 4-fold line of extent 1.375 and 5-phase corners. slab-line 3D seed 2: B30 in 2 parts (B merge at step 34). 2D sq2-checker with jitter 1e-2, seed 4: 2 merges at step 1.
claims.refuteBy: Re-run sq2-checker 3D seed 1 and slab-line 3D seed 2 with a connected-components check after every merge: if no phase ever has more than one part, the claim is wrong.

claims.statement: A chain of three bubbles (A|B|A) has a neutral mode. Both outer arcs of the middle bubble lie on one circle, so rotating an end bubble about that circle's centre changes neither length nor any area. Chain shapes form a one-parameter family; bending is free until the ends touch and could then unite.
claims.numbers: From the solver polylines: B's outer arcs have centres (1.5, 0.502) and (1.5, 0.498), radius 0.69810 and 0.69808. Pressures are A 1.5650 and B 1.4345; 1/R_B = 1.4325. The wall radius fits 7.73 against 1/(pA − pB) = 7.66.
claims.refuteBy: A solver or engine run started from a bent A|B|A chain that returns to straight, or one whose energy depends on the bend angle by more than the discretisation error (about 1e-4).

claims.statement: Two different materials touching only along an edge (diag-edge-diff) is not decided by physics: both separating and adhering lower the energy. Steepest descent separates; adhesion leads to the lower-energy double bubble. The engine's choice depends on the blur: it adheres at s_b 0.2 and separates at s_b 0.1.
claims.numbers: Solver: separate, E 7.0907. Equal double bubble: 6.359 (exact.mjs). Split rates at the X: separate 1.414, adhere 0.414. Engine at s_b 0.2: adheres in 2D (n32, n64, n128; jitter 0 and 1e-3: 9/9) and in 3D (n16, 2/2). At s_b 0.1, n64: separates, distance 0.0066/0.019 to the separated solution.
claims.refuteBy: An s_b 0.2 engine run that separates diag-edge-diff, or an s_b 0.1 run that adheres.

claims.statement: Pattern (a) holds for physics, with qualifications: the free equilibrium is set by the contact graph after lattice junctions are resolved by the pressure rule (C6, C11) and by the volumes, up to neutral modes (C10). It is not unique at exact ties. The face-contact graph alone does not decide. The engine adds about 5% dependence on block arrangement through pinning.
claims.numbers: Same volumes 1:2 in four arrangements (row-ABB, L-ABB, L3-AAB, row-AAB): r1 0.670–0.676, r2 0.805–0.810, a 0.640–0.652. V3 spheres (line3, L3, pillar3): λ 0.1778 / 0.1778 / 0.1789. Counterexamples to the face graph alone: line3-ABA stays a chain while L3-ABA unites its A's (A2|B1); line3-ABC is a chain while L3-ABC is a triple bubble. Engine arrangement dependence: sq2-AABB against row-AABB, a 0.768 / 0.746 and length 2.372 / 2.498.
claims.refuteBy: Two block arrangements with the same contact graph after junction resolution and the same volumes whose exact (solver) equilibria differ by more than the neutral modes.

claims.statement: Pattern (c): for small clusters the free result is predictable without simulating. One cluster becomes a sphere of radius (3V/4π)^(1/3). Two face-touching clusters become the standard double bubble of the two volumes (exact.mjs: outer radii meeting at 120°, wall radius r1·r2/(r2 − r1) bulging into the larger bubble). Pressure goes as 1/R, and the smaller bubble has the higher pressure. This prediction fails for clusters beyond the pinning radius.
claims.numbers: For 15 two-cluster configurations with V ≤ 8 (n16): outer radii within −0.7% to +5.5% of exact, junction radius within +1.6% to +10.2%, λ within 4% of 2/r·s_b/√(2π). Pinned outliers: slab-dot (B24) r1 +65%; ball-AB at n12 r1 +13%.
claims.refuteBy: A two-cluster configuration with V ≤ 7 whose engine (n16, s 0.2) outer radii differ from the exact double bubble of the same volumes by more than 6%.

claims.statement: Pattern (b): in the FREE engine results, Plateau structure (sheets, triple lines, isolated 4-phase points) holds for 42 of 44 configurations. Junctions of four or more bodies appear as 4-fold lines and 5-phase corners only where four bodies sat symmetrically around a lattice edge (sq2-ABCD in both seeds, sq2-checker in seed 1). Eight blocks around a lattice vertex (cube2-checker, cube2-octants) always resolved.
claims.numbers: The census counts by connected component. Isolated points: L3-ABC 2, sq2-AABC 2, cube2-octants 5 (extent ≤ 0.063). Lines: sq2-ABCD extent 1.25 with hist[5] = 2; sq2-checker seed 1 extent 1.375. All other configurations have no corner with ≥ 4 bodies.
claims.refuteBy: Re-run the census (freecat.mjs) on any of the 42 'clean' configurations and find a 4-body component with extent > 0.25 block, or find a 4-fold line in the exact solver.

claims.statement: Seams between different materials stay on block faces in the engine at its default resolution, even where physics moves them by about 0.1 block. Examples: in 2D at n32 the A|B wall of a 1:2 double bubble and both walls of A|B|A stay on lattice lines, and in 3D the 1:2 wall stays exactly planar. This is pinning (C5), not physics, so 'boundaries stay on the lattice' in engine pictures must not be read as a bubble law.
claims.numbers: row-ABB 2D n32: mean / max 0.059/0.154 from exact, against 0.003/0.011 at n128. line3-ABA: 0.060/0.110 at n32, 0.005/0.014 at n128. Exact walls sit at x = 1.107 and 1.893 (solver junctions). 3D row-ABB wall plane rms 0 at n12, 16, 24 and 32.
claims.refuteBy: A 2D n32 s_b 0.2 run of row-ABB whose A|B wall is off the lattice line x = 1 by at least 0.1 block, matching the exact wall.

optimizations.idea: Skip simulation for small free clusters: compute the cluster graph and volumes, then place closed-form shapes (a sphere for one cluster, the standard double bubble from exact.mjs for two face-touching clusters).
optimizations.gain: A 1-D root find replaces 20–130 MBO steps (0.5–7 s per configuration at n16, doubles/results.json 'ms'). It is at least as accurate as the engine for V ≤ 8 and better beyond the pinning radius, where the engine is wrong by 13–65%.
optimizations.risks: Valid only for the FREE regime, which destroys block shapes and is not a terrain look. Three or more clusters need the triple-bubble and chain solutions; chains have a neutral bending mode (C10). Lattice four-fold junctions must be resolved first (C6).

optimizations.idea: Resolve every lattice four-fold junction before any smoothing with the pressure rule: connect the diagonal pair with the higher pressure (the smaller cluster; air = 0). Same material therefore always connects across an air diagonal at a shared edge. Same-material vertex-only contact separates. Exact ties get an explicit, deterministic design choice, such as the lower material id. This could be a per-corner table in the style of the bevel rule (PLAN.md 7.9) with a cluster-size comparison.
optimizations.gain: It removes the engine's persisting X junctions (C7) and its seed dependence at ties (C9), and it matches exact physics in every unequal case tested (16/16 2D and 4/4 3D runs, plus diag-edge, L3-ABC and slab-line). For the owner's painted-diagonal case it decides deterministically whether the line stays continuous.
optimizations.risks: Pressure needs cluster size, which is non-local; a mesher job only sees a 38³ or 52³ region, so a local proxy (inference) would be needed and is untested. The rule can pick a higher-energy end state than the global minimum (C8), but that is what physics does. Ties and the different-material edge contact (C11) are design decisions, not physics.

optimizations.idea: Choose engine settings by the pinning law. R_pin = 2·s_b²·n must exceed the radius of the largest bubble that should round. Raising s_b from 0.2 to 0.3 at n 16 raises R_pin from 1.28 to 2.88 at no extra grid cost. A stall detector should flag runs that stop with changes = 0 while some bubble has R > R_pin.
optimizations.gain: For the 64-block cube at n16, radial spread falls from 0.241 to 0.030 by changing s_b from 0.2 to 0.3. This avoids raising n, where cost grows as n³ (1.2 M cell cap).
optimizations.risks: A larger s_b widens the junction error: the junction circle grows to +10–12% and the air angle to about 130° (C2, C3). A smaller s_b pins earlier. There is no setting that is both unpinned and junction-exact at affordable n.

optimizations.idea: Two small engine fixes. After every merge, run a connected-components pass and re-split any phase that has come apart. Break exact symmetric X junctions deliberately, either by applying the pressure rule or by flipping one sub-cell toward the higher-pressure pair, instead of relying on jitter.
optimizations.gain: It removes the non-physical states seen in sq2-checker seed 1, slab-line seed 2 and sq2-ABCD (both seeds, 2D up to n128), making FREE results Plateau-clean.
optimizations.risks: Re-splitting changes phase bookkeeping (targets, λ). A forced X split must choose an option at exact ties, which is a design choice.

optimizations.idea: Use the independent 2D solver (foam2d.mjs) as ground truth for regression tests of any smoothing or seam rule evaluated on 2D slices.
optimizations.gain: Energy error 5e-5 at h 0.02, junction angles of 120 ± 0.09°, pressures within 0.03%, and 1–7 s per small case. It decides lattice-junction topology explicitly and reports both options.
optimizations.risks: 2D only. Merging through an air gap (bubbles approaching without a shared film) is detected but not performed. It is research code, not deterministic across browsers.

openQuestions: Is the too-wide air angle (C3) intrinsic to volume-constrained threshold dynamics with an unconstrained air phase? A 2D run at s_b 0.05 with n ≥ 256 would separate the blur effect from pinning.
Would a one-sub-cell seed toward either diagonal pair let the engine relax sq2-ABCD to its true minimum, and does it then reproduce the exact pressures (1.441 / 1.357)?

Physics does not decide two cases: different materials touching only along an edge (separate or adhere), and exact checkerboard ties. Which choice does the owner want for painted seams? It must be stated as a rule.
How should the pressure rule (C6) be approximated locally inside a mesher job, which sees only a 38³ or 52³ region, when the deciding cluster sizes are non-local?
3D neutral modes: does a slightly bent line3-ABA chain stay bent in the engine, and does a bend that lets the end bubbles touch make them unite?
The tetrahedral 109.47° angle needs a better 3D measurement (n ≥ 48 in a cropped box, or a 3D surface solver) to test it to ±2°.

results.summary: I swept 17 configurations: the 15 in the mission, sq2-same, and a new slab-halves with one straight A|B seam. They ran under 15 regimes (BLOCKS, FID-k ×5, FID-0.15 with g 0.5 and 1.5, CAGE-r ×3, FINITE-T ×3, FREE) on the unchanged engine at n 16. I measured rounding, seam grooves, flatness, volume, convergence, the constraint scenes and diagonal-contact union, and checked key numbers at n 12/20/24 and in 2D at n 32/64/128. No regime on the mission's list is both visibly rounder than the blocks and keeps the 1×2 tunnel's 0.70 × 1.90 opening (cell-exact on labels). FID-0.25 and FID-0.4 keep it but do not change the blocks at all (Δ ≤ 0.006); every moving regime closes it, partly or fully. The cause is the per-cluster volume constraint: volume freed by rounding convex edges goes into concavities and faces. It is non-local: attaching a bar 4 or more blocks away closes the FID-0.15 tunnel (clear height 1.17 → 0), while the same bar detached changes nothing. Turning volume off instead deletes single blocks, pillars and rings. An engine copy (src/mbo-look.mjs, beyond the mission's list) keeps volume and fidelity, bounds the solid/air surface with a PLAN §7.4-style box (0.125 horizontal, 0 vertical, eroded core 0.25), and lets paint move almost freely (kMat 0.02). That gives two candidates, BOX0-PAINT-0.1-0.02 and BOX0-PAINT-0.15-0.02. Both pass every constraint scene, are visibly rounded, and turn the owner's hard case (a painted 1-wide diagonal) into one straight band while flat ground stays exactly flat. In anchored regimes, seams between materials stay colour, not grooves: Neumann's angles appear only in free or caged runs at fine resolution (2D double bubble 90.6° / 107.1° / 116.9° at n 32/64/128 against 120°). On union: diagonal edge contacts in air unite in every moving regime, corner-only contacts never do, and painted diagonals end connected only where the paint can move. The harness refused to write REPORT.md, so the full report is this structured result. The evidence is in results/*.json, results/table-*.md, results/union-table.md, logs/ and sheets/ under the team folder.

The render field rounds raw blocks itself (edge R 0.20, faces out 0.03), so 'blocks' pictures already look rounded, and D-field constraint checks fail for reasons unrelated to the physics.

In anchored FID regimes (k ≥ 0.1), a flat A|B seam stays flat: depth ≤ 0.0625 on the labels in 3D at n 16, and 0.006 in 2D at n 64/128 for FID-0.15. Material seams remain colour, not geometry.

Union of same-material diagonal contacts (jitter 0, and jitter 1e-3 with seeds 1–3), stated as final connectivity:

optimizations.idea: Bound the solid/air surface with a PLAN §7.4-style per-axis box (growth into air ≤ 0.15 horizontally, ≤ 0.05 or 0 vertically; eroded core always solid) instead of a soft anchor. Keep volume per cluster so small features keep their size.
optimizations.gain: The constraints hold by construction (tunnel 2.0 × 0.75 at n 16 and 1.90 × 0.70 with the exact caps at n 20; flat ground exact) while the rounding stays at the FID-0.1/0.15 level. The candidates' Δ mean (0.047–0.080) is close to plain FID-0.15 (0.067).
optimizations.risks: Measured at n 16 (box quantised) except the tunnel at n 20. Vertical faces still bulge up to 0.125. Per-cluster volume coupling remains (bounded by the box).

optimizations.idea: Solve paint and shape separately. With a low paint fidelity (kMat ≈ 0.02) the material partition relaxes into smooth films (straight diagonal bands, round dots, S-curved seams on steps) while the surface stays held. Paint could be computed as a surface-confined 2D problem on the top-surface material map (inference).
optimizations.gain: Solves the painted-diagonal hard case (band SD 0.409 → 0.050) with no geometric change to flat ground. A 2D paint solve would touch only surface cells (inference).
optimizations.risks: The mesh needs a way to represent sub-quad material boundaries; today vertices split per (corner, material). Paint volume is still a per-cluster constraint.

optimizations.idea: Replace per-cluster volume conservation with a local one (per block or per neighbourhood), so the result depends only on a bounded apron and can be meshed chunk by chunk or baked into a per-corner table, as the bevel's 256-entry table is.
optimizations.gain: Removes the measured non-local coupling (4.3 block³ change from a bar at least 4 blocks away under FID-0.15; 0.05–0.19 block³ at 2.5 or more blocks for the candidates). Makes a deterministic, apron-bounded rule possible.
optimizations.risks: Untested. Dropping volume entirely makes features vanish (NV-FID-0.15 Δ 1.0), so the local substitute must still protect small features.

optimizations.idea: Use the union pattern as a topology rule: same-material edge contacts in air connect (a neck); corner-only contacts stay separate; painted diagonals inside solid connect when paint is free; symmetric X junctions need a deterministic tie rule.
optimizations.gain: A table-friendly rule that matches the bubble model in every moving regime tested. It differs from the current mesher, where diagonal-only contacts stay pinched (PLAN §7.2).
optimizations.risks: The checkerboard outcome depends on the seed in CAGE and FREE (and layered in 3D), so any game rule is a choice, not physics. Changing pinching changes mesh topology and the goldens.

openQuestions: Can BOX0-PAINT be baked into a local per-corner rule? The surface changes sit within about 0.5 block of edges and seams (Δ mean 0.047–0.080), but λ couples the whole cluster; a local volume substitute is untested.
How should smooth paint boundaries (straight diagonal bands, round dots) be represented in the mesh, given vertices split per (corner, material)?

Does the owner want grooves at material seams? Anchored regimes give colour-only seams; grooves need FID ≤ 0.05, FINITE or a cage, all of which break constraints unless the groove is added inside a box (untested).
3D checkerboard X junctions can unite both pairs by layering (FREE seed 2). Which outcome should a game rule pick, given it depends on the seed?
Why does CAGE-0.25 with g 1.5 separate A from B with an air gap in 2D (n 64), when g < 2 should keep the film? Pinning, or a real instability of a squeezed contact?

All scenes float in air (no ground or periodic boundary). The FREE and terrain-step numbers are partly artefacts of that; the tunnel and locality results come from inside one cluster and should not depend on it (inference).

The candidates were swept over the catalogue only at n 16, where the box is quantised to 0.125 / 0. Only the tunnel was checked at n 20 with the exact 0.15 / 0.05 caps. Do the looks and constraints hold at finer n?

The FID-k look is set by MBO pinning at s 0.2, not by k alone: a continuum estimate gives a fillet radius of about 0.53 at k 0.15 against an edge Req of 0.17 measured (inference). Another solver given the same k would give a different look.

results.summary:
I couldn't write REPORT.md: the harness refuses report .md files from subagents. This result is the report. Everything else is saved and backed up: scripts in src/, numbers in res/ and logs/, 58 images in img/, 4 contact sheets in sheets/, and a reference cache in refcache/.

What I did:
- Checked the engine's first MBO step against an analytic sum of per-block kernels.
- Ran the physics references FID-0.15, FINITE-4 and FINITE-2 on all 36 catalogue configurations, plus FREE on 7 small ones. n = 16, except n = 12 for ball-r2 and ball-AB.
- Built local one-step models on the same grids and measured surface distance, seam distance and volume error against those references.
- Turned the best model into a deterministic vertex-placement rule for surface-nets corners, using only + - * /. Timed it on generated chunks next to the repo mesher, bundled from HEAD c27fa8b.

Headline findings:
1. One MBO step from the blocks is exactly a metaball sum, to 8e-8.
2. Threshold 1/2 shrinks small clusters: one block keeps 0.665 of its volume at sigma 0.2 and vanishes only above sigma 0.40. Restoring volume with a per-material shift (lambda) gives a mean surface distance to FID-0.15 of 0.018 blocks. A purely local lambda rule (count of same-material blocks in the 3x3x3) gives 0.019, with 1.6 % mean volume error.
3. T engine steps behave like one step at sigma*sqrt(T); the evidence is T = 2 and T = 4.
4. Compact polynomial kernels cost almost no accuracy. With the box*tent kernel at sigma 0.2, a corner's vertex depends only on its 8 blocks (plus n27 for lambda).
5. The vertex rule costs about 2–8 ms per chunk, against 4–25 ms for the whole repo mesher on the same 38^3 inputs. It is seam-exact, but plain Newton fails to converge at 0.4 % of corners.

Main caveat: one vertex per lattice corner cannot hold 'flat face plus rounded edge'. Placing vertices on the physical surface (0.032 from it, against 0.15 for cubes) drags the flat quads inward, so against FID plain cubes give the smaller mesh error (0.034 against 0.113). The rule only wins on large or strongly rounded shapes.

Feature checks:
- Survive in the cheap model: seamless union, groove depth at material seams, and short-time junction angles.
- Lost or changed: FID's concave fill, which needs about 10 iterations; diagonal union in the mesh (topology keeps it pinched); and the physics' wall between diagonal different-material blocks.
- The physics itself closes the 1x2 tunnel to 1.21–1.43 blocks high, and the vertex rule gives 1.73. Both are below the required 1.90, so the existing §7.4 constraint box would have to apply after the rule.

claims.statement: One MBO step from the blocks is a metaball model. In the engine's first step, each cluster's blurred indicator P.u equals the sum over its blocks of the separable kernel built from the engine's discrete Gaussian, to float32 precision. It differs from the continuum erf kernel k(t) = (erf((t+1/2)/(sqrt2 sigma)) - erf((t-1/2)/(sqrt2 sigma)))/2, sigma = s/n = 0.2, only by discretisation.
claims.numbers: 10 configurations, up to 1.09 M cells. Engine against discrete kernel in f64: max 8.1e-8. Engine against erf continuum: max 0.0044, rms at most 0.0010. Step-1 labels rebuilt from the analytic fields with the engine's lambdas differ only where the two best costs are within 0.0029 (0–96 cells; 5,292 of 143,712 in slab-line; 9,496 of 304,724 in terrain-step).
claims.refuteBy: Run t1.mjs on any configuration at n = 16, s = 3.2 and find max |P.u - discrete sum| > 1e-6, or max |P.u - erf sum| > 0.01.

claims.statement: In the engine's per-step volume solve, large flat clusters settle on lambda = 0.12479. That value puts the threshold exactly on the first outside sub-cell layer of a flat face, so whole face layers become near-ties. This is a numerical property of the cell-quantile volume solve, not physics.
claims.numbers: lambda = 0.12479 for slab-line's B clusters and all three terrain-step clusters at step 1. The outside-cell value of u at a face is about 0.4378, and (1 - 0.12479)/2 = 0.4376 (inference). The label mismatches cluster there.
claims.refuteBy: Print the step-1 margins per cell for terrain-step and show that the mismatching cells are not in the first sub-cell layer outside flat faces, or that lambda does not jump in steps when the flat-face area changes.

claims.statement: One blur of the blocks thresholded at 1/2 (lambda 0) shrinks small clusters and makes single blocks vanish only above sigma about 0.40. At the engine's sigma 0.2 a single block keeps two thirds of its volume.
claims.numbers: Fraction of volume kept at sigma 0.2: single 0.665, pair 0.764, line of 3 0.796, 2x2 0.848, 2x2x2 0.907, ball r 2.2 0.948. At sigma 0.40: single 0, pair 0.17, 2x2x2 0.66. Analytic vanishing sigma 0.3956.
claims.refuteBy: Compute the {2u > 1} volume of one block's erf-kernel field at sigma 0.2 on a fine grid and get a fraction outside 0.64–0.69, or find the block still present at sigma 0.41.

claims.statement: A one-step metaball model with volume restored by one lambda per material reproduces the FID-0.15 physics surface to a mean distance of about 0.02 blocks over the 36-configuration catalogue. Restoring volume is what matters: lambda 0 is 3.5 times worse.

Surface mean / mean p95 / worst p95, with mean and worst |volume error|:
- Bx-g20: 0.0180 / 0.056 / 0.203; volume 0.000 / 0.003
- A0-g20: 0.0622 / 0.112 / 0.259; volume 0.185 / 0.338
- Bc15-g20: 0.0278; volume 0.067 / 0.166
Seam mean 0.006–0.009.

claims.statement: T engine steps from the blocks (FINITE-T) are approximated by a single volume-kept step at sigma about 0.2*sqrt(T).
claims.numbers:
Surface mean against FINITE-4, by one-step sigma: 0.30 → 0.0244, 0.35 → 0.0141, 0.40 → 0.0101 (best), 0.45 → 0.0184, 0.50 → 0.0317.
Against FINITE-2: 0.20 → 0.0255, 0.25 → 0.0144, 0.30 → 0.0072 (best tested), 0.35 → 0.0137.
Code check: 4 iterated steps reproduce FINITE-4 to 0.0067.

claims.statement: The volume shift can be estimated locally. Each block gets lambda_b = a + b((27 - n27_b)/26)^4, where n27_b is the count of same-material blocks in its 3x3x3; the values are blended by the same kernel. At sigma 0.2 this keeps volume to about 2 % and gives nearly the oracle's surface accuracy, including on held-out larger configurations. At sigma 0.4 it does not.
claims.numbers:
Fit: a = 0.0498, b = 0.1883, rmse 0.022 over 65 per-material lambdas in the range 0.071–0.271.
Bl-g20 against FID: surface mean 0.0192, volume error mean 1.6 %, worst 8.2 %.
Holdout (fitted on configurations of at most 12 blocks, tested on the 7 larger ones): volume 2.4 % mean, 5.2 % worst; surface 0.0266 against 0.0258 for the exact oracle.
Bl-g40 against FINITE-4: volume 8.6 % mean, 50 % worst.
claims.refuteBy: Apply the g20 rule to generated terrain or new configurations (overhangs, thin walls, mixed slabs) and find volume errors above 10 % for clusters of more than 12 blocks.

claims.statement: The concave fillets of FID-0.15 come from iterating to its fixed point. One step does not reproduce them; repeated fidelity steps converge toward them.
claims.numbers: Same 10 configurations, surface mean / mean p95: 2 steps 0.0266 / 0.107; 4 steps 0.0222 / 0.084; 10 steps 0.0166 / 0.053; one step (Bx-g20) 0.0246 / 0.098. On stairs alone, p95 goes 0.145 → 0.048 from 2 to 10 steps. The FID references took 8–41 steps.

claims.statement: Compact piecewise-polynomial kernels (box convolved with a B-spline of the same variance) replace the erf kernel at almost no cost in accuracy. With the box*tent kernel at sigma <= 0.204, the field inside a lattice corner's cell depends only on that corner's 8 blocks: it is trilinear interpolation of the 8 occupancies in coordinates warped by the quadratic smoothstep w(s) over [-h, h], h = sigma*sqrt6.
claims.numbers:
Against FID with local lambda, surface mean: Gaussian 0.0192, b3 0.0201, b2 0.0206, b1 0.0208. Against FINITE-4 with exact lambda: Gaussian 0.0101, b3 0.0111.
b1 support at sigma 0.2 is 0.990 blocks (computed). The 8-block property follows from support < 1 (derivation).

claims.statement: The one-step model as a surface-nets vertex rule (b1 kernel, local lambda, 4 Newton steps, quantised to 1/256) costs about the same per chunk as the repo mesher's vertex work. It needs an apron of 2, so it fits the 38³ region. With a constant lambda, single-material corners reduce to a 256-entry table.
claims.numbers:
Minimum time per chunk, two runs on a loaded machine:
- bub-b1 local: 2.1–3.2 ms on surface chunks (1.3k–2.5k corners), 5.6–7.8 ms on mixed and cave chunks (6.2k–8.5k corners), with one outlier at 11.4.
- b3 (64 blocks): 7–52 ms.
- Table floor (scanning 33³ corners): 0.7–1.5 ms.
- Repo mesher, whole mesh, same inputs: 4.1–24.5 ms.
- Multi-material corners per chunk: 0–900.
- Physics engine step at 1.09 M cells: 427 ms (t1 log).
claims.refuteBy: Time bubbleVertices (b1, local lambda) on the same chunks in a quiet Node session and get more than 10 ms on the cave chunks, or show that shared corners differ when the apron is 2.

claims.statement: The vertex rule gives identical offsets on both sides of a chunk seam because it reads only blocks within the 38³ region. Plain Newton does not converge at a small set of corners, mostly two-material corners with 7 solid blocks. A safeguarded line search along the corner gradient always converges, at about 2.5 times the cost.
claims.numbers:
Seams: 558 shared corners over 5 chunk pairs, 0 mismatches, for b1 and b3; same machine and JS engine only.
Newton: 4 against 16 iterations differ by more than 1/256 at 65 of 17,284 corners, max 0.96 block. 51 of those are 7-solid two-material corners.
Line search: 14 against 40 bisections, 0 corners differ by more than 1/256. Cost 13–19 ms on cave chunks.
claims.refuteBy: Find a shared corner with different offsets in two adjacent chunks, or a corner where the line solver at 14 bisections differs from 40 by more than 1/256.

claims.statement: With one vertex per lattice corner, putting vertices on the physical surface does not minimise mesh error. Against FID-0.15, plain cube corners give the smallest quad-surface error, because flat quads between on-surface vertices cut through flat faces that have rounded edges. On-surface vertices win only for large or strongly rounded shapes.

Mean distance over 36 configurations, vertex / quad patch:
- Against FID-0.15: bub-b1 0.032 / 0.113; cube 0.150 / 0.034; bevel 0.187 / 0.230; hints (binary placed blocks) 0.294 / 0.329.
- Against FINITE-4: bub-b1 0.068 / 0.105; cube 0.223 / 0.078; bub-b1 with offsets x 0.5: 0.144 / 0.072.
- The 8 large configurations against FINITE-4, patch only: bub-b1 0.062, cube 0.097, bevel 0.173.

claims.statement: Seamless union of same-material blocks and the groove at different-material seams both survive in the cheap model, with the groove's depth close to the physics. In a surface-nets mesh the groove can only be one quad wide on each side of the seam.

pair-diff dip: FID 0.050, FINITE-4 0.068, FREE 0.052; models 0.042–0.058.

They unite in the one-step field only when lambda > 0, and then through a thinner neck. They can never unite in the surface-nets mesh, because its topology keeps diagonal contacts pinched. Between different materials, the physics presses the blocks into a shared wall that the sigma-0.2 model barely forms.

The sigma-0.2 one-step field keeps the tunnel, but the b1 vertex rule alone lowers the clearance to 1.73, so the §7.4 constraint box would still have to apply after it. optimizations.idea: Replace the multi-step physics with one blur of the blocks: a separable sum of per-block kernels with per-material sums and the engine's least-psi rule, plus a volume shift lambda. For shape-keeping use sigma 0.2. For a T-step relaxation look use sigma 0.2*sqrt(T).
optimizations.gain: Surface within 0.018–0.021 mean of FID-0.15, and within 0.010 of FINITE-4 at sigma 0.4. No iteration, no global solve if the local lambda is used. An engine step costs 427 ms at 1.09 M cells; the model is a few kernel evaluations per point.
optimizations.risks: No concave fill (FID's fixed point), so worst p95 is 0.13–0.20 on concave shapes. The local lambda fails at sigma 0.4 (50 % worst volume error). Fitted on the 36-configuration catalogue only.

optimizations.idea: Use the box*tent (b1) kernel at sigma 0.2 as a surface-nets vertex rule. Inside each corner's cell the field is warped trilinear interpolation of its 8 blocks, plus a local lambda from n27, so only + - * / are needed and the apron is 2.
optimizations.gain: 2–8 ms per 38³ chunk in Node, compared with 4–25 ms for the whole repo mesher. Seam-exact (0 of 558 shared corners differ). Vertices sit 0.032 mean from the FID surface, against 0.187 for bevel.
optimizations.risks: Flat quads between on-surface vertices give a larger patch error than plain cubes against FID (0.113 against 0.034). Newton fails to converge at 0.4 % of corners; the line solver fixes that at about 2.5x the cost. Tunnel height drops to 1.73, so the §7.4 constraint box is still needed.

optimizations.idea: Precompute the vertex offsets as tables. With a constant lambda: 256 entries for single-material corners, and a material-partition table of at most Bell(9) = 21,147 patterns (about 63 KB as int8) for mixed corners. The tables can be built offline with the robust line solver.
optimizations.gain: 0.7–1.5 ms per chunk (measured scan-plus-lookup floor). Removes the convergence problem from runtime.
optimizations.risks: A constant lambda gives 4–7 % mean volume error on the catalogue (Bc12/Bc15 rows). The partition table is inferred, not built or timed; multi-material corners are up to 900 per surface chunk.

optimizations.idea: Scale the vertex offsets (alpha about 0.5) to trade vertex accuracy for quad-surface accuracy on strongly rounded targets.
optimizations.gain: Against FINITE-4, patch error 0.072, against 0.078 for cubes and 0.105 for unscaled offsets.
optimizations.risks: Only three alpha values were tried. A per-mask optimised table might do better. Against FID, cubes still win.

openQuestions: REPORT.md was not written. The harness refused report .md files from subagents, so this structured result is the report. Could the orchestrator write REPORT.md from it, or allow the file?
Which vertex placement minimises the quad-patch error rather than the vertex error? A per-mask table fitted to the physics might beat both cubes and on-surface vertices.

Which physics regime should the game target? FID-0.15 keeps block shapes but closes 1x2 tunnels to 1.21 high; FINITE-4 rounds strongly. sigma in the cheap model is the dial (sigma*sqrt(T)). This is the owner's look decision.
Can a local term reproduce FID's concave fill, for example the max of two one-step fields at different sigma? Not tried.
Cross-browser determinism of the vertex rule was not tested; only same-engine seams were. The lambda table and b1 constants would need to be frozen as rationals.

Timing ran on a machine shared with other runs, with up to 50 % spread between runs. The repo mesher itself measured 14–25 ms on heavy cave chunks here. Production timing belongs in the repo's own profile test.
The sigma*sqrt(T) scaling rests on T = 2 and T = 4 only.
The groove depth and junction angles were measured on the engine's D field, which rounds creases by about 0.1. They should be re-measured on labels at n = 32.
