results.summary:
Team 'local' measured how block clusters combine in the shared MBO bubble engine. The work used about 900 3D runs: n = 12 for 14×2×5 slabs, n = 16 for the Task 4 contact scenes. It covered FID-0.15, FID-0.05, FINITE-4, CAGE-0.25, FREE and volume:false controls. Each run records three measures: labels (quantised at 1/n), D0 (the labels re-blurred with λ = 0, a purely local smooth field) and the renderer's own field D.

Headline: the bubble pressure λ (the volume constraint) is the only long-range carrier. Without it, a one-block add, remove, recolour or bridge changes labels only within 0–0.475 block of that block, and a probe 2 or more blocks away does not change at all. With it, the response reaches the whole cluster whenever λ changes. In this engine that response comes as whole sub-cell terraces (multiples of 1/12 block), placed where flat-face cells tie, rather than as a decaying tail. In three regimes it releases volume deficits the bases had stored (CAGE-0.25: the top face rises 0.25 at every distance).

The local near field has compact support: a FID-0.15 bump's skirt ends by 1.0 block, pits and inclusions by 0.25, the seam position by 0.5. Convex edges, inclusions and straight seams take the same shape in every cluster tested. A straight seam does not move at all in FID/FINITE (labels flat at n = 12 and 16); its groove is the renderer's blur of the unmoved blocks, which I give in closed form and which matches a discrete model to 4.75e-6 block. Concave features and thin attached features do depend on the whole cluster: under CAGE a 1×1 pillar's width falls 1.06 → 0.69 → 0.49 as the plate it stands on grows, and FID-0.05 drains an attached pillar completely. Superposition is exact only where λ stays fixed (FINITE-4, features 2 or more blocks apart).

At ambiguous contacts the smaller pair unites (FINITE-4, CAGE, FREE, and FID-0.05 for large size ratios). Equal sizes give no union with jitter 0 and with reversed block order, so there is no tie-break bias. Edge contacts with air always unite, corner-only contacts never do, and FID-0.15 never resolves an X. A local rule, "minority in a 4×4×3 window connects; ties none; air-X connects; corner never", matches the physics in 21/21 configurations for FINITE-4, 20/21 CAGE, 19/20 FREE, 19/21 FID-0.05 and 10/21 FID-0.15. It keeps the painted diagonal line continuous, as every regime except FID-0.15 does.

REPORT.md was not written: the harness blocks report files from subagents. The full report is this structured result. Every number is in results JSON and logs under teams/local/ (backed up to <backup>/teams/local/). The engine copy lib/mbo-box.mjs adds a shared-grid bbox, records the dynamics λ before finish(), adds a forced-union option and adds finishLocal(); the README is followed otherwise.

claims.statement: Without the volume constraint (volume:false), a one-block change is strictly local, and that includes a bridging block. Label changes stay within 0 to 0.475 block of the changed block, and D0 at a probe 2 or more blocks away changes by exactly 0.
claims.numbers: 14x2x5 A slab, n=12. FID-0.15-novol add/remove: 328 cells change, all inside the changed block (max distance 0); recolour: the B inclusion is erased (0 diffs). FINITE-4-novol: max distance 0.375 (add/remove), 0.208 (recolour). D0 probe change at d=2,4,8: 0 in every novol run. Bridge, FID-0.15-novol: max distance 0.475 (A bridge), 0.243 (B bridge); far dTop0 = 0. CAGE-0.25-novol did not converge in 300 steps (excluded). FID-0.05-novol erases the whole slab, so it is no control.
claims.refuteBy: Repeat any converged volume:false perturbation on this slab or a larger one (n=12 or 16). A label change more than 0.5 block from the changed block, or a non-zero D0 change at a probe 2 or more blocks away, refutes it.

claims.statement: With volume:true, λ carries influence across the whole cluster, and only when the perturbation changes λ. Far from the change the response is quantised into whole sub-cell terraces (multiples of 1/n block) on flat faces; there is no smooth decaying tail. FID-0.15 converges by placing its rounding loss in a one-layer plateau patch on the top and bottom faces. Any bump removes that patch, wherever the bump is.
claims.numbers: FID-0.15 base: volume exactly 140, λ 0.17529, 45 steps; plateau +1/12 on the centre line from x = 4.875 to 9.125, on top and bottom. A bump at any d moves λ to 0.13277 and removes the plateau; far label change 0.083 (1216 cells beyond 2.5 blocks). Remove: λ → 0.1078, 1404 far cells. Recolour: λ_A → 0.20705, 1876 far cells. Changes reach up to 12 blocks away. Far amplitudes seen: 0.083, 0.167, 0.25 (= 1, 2, 3 × 1/12). Where λ is unchanged the response is local: FINITE-4 remove/recolour keep λ 0.16629 and change labels ≤ 0.208 block; CAGE remove changes only pit cells. The tie mechanism is an inference from the equal margins of flat faces.
claims.refuteBy: Re-run the base and the d=6 bump at n=16 and n=24 on the same blocks. If the far-field amplitude stays 0.083 block instead of 1/n, or changes in sub-layer amounts, the quantisation explanation fails. A perturbation that changes λ with no label change beyond 2.5 blocks also refutes it.

claims.statement: FID-0.05, FINITE-4 and CAGE-0.25 bases stop with a volume deficit, λ pinned at a tie. One new concave site (a bump) releases the stored deficit across the whole cluster. In a continuum model the same deficit would shift the surface only about ΔV/area.
claims.numbers: Base volumes of 140: FID-0.05 139.241 (λ 0.21629, 7 steps), FINITE-4 138 (λ 0.16629), CAGE-0.25 136.083 (λ 0.16629, 84 steps). One bump: CAGE top face +0.25 (the cage limit) at every d, 24432 cells changed beyond 2.5 blocks; FID-0.05 mound with a 3.5–5 block skirt, 11800 far cells; probe D0 0.53/0.34/0.17/0.03/0 at d = 1/2/3/4/≥6. Continuum estimate for the CAGE base, 3.92/216 ≈ 0.018 block, is inference.
claims.refuteBy: Use a volume solver that splits tied flat-face layers (a partial layer) so the bases reach 140. If the bump response is then still cluster-wide at more than 1/64, the deficit-release mechanism is wrong.

claims.statement: With volume on, the near-field response to one block has compact support (exactly zero past a cutoff), so d* hardly depends on the tolerance. Radii are measured contiguously from the changed block along the slab's centre line in D0, in runs where no terrace touches the change.
claims.numbers: d* at 1/256 · 1/64 · 1/16 (0.25-block sampling, +0.125). FID-0.15: bump 1.0 · 0.75 · 0.75; pit 0.25 · 0 · 0; inclusion 0.25 · 0 · 0. FINITE-4: bump 2.25 · 2.0 · 2.0 (a terrace ring); pit and inclusion 0.25 · 0.25 · 0. FID-0.05 bump ≥ 3.5. CAGE add/recolour: whole cluster. FID-0.15 bump skirt in D0 at 0.125/0.375/0.625/0.875/1.125 block from its face: 0.370/0.187/0.084/0.012/0.
claims.refuteBy: Sample the same runs on a 2D grid of probes, or repeat at n=16. A terrace-free D0 change above 1/256 more than 1.125 block from a FID-0.15 bump, or more than 0.375 from a FID-0.15 pit or inclusion, refutes it.

claims.statement: The position of a straight A|B seam is local. Recolouring one block to touch the seam moves the seam within 0.5 block (FID-0.15) or 0.75 (FID-0.05, FINITE-4). CAGE-0.25 is the exception: there the whole seam shifts one sub-cell.
claims.numbers: 14x2x4 A|B slab, seam z at y=1.5 in D0. d* at 1/256 · 1/64 · 1/16: FID-0.15 0.5 · 0.25 · 0.25; FID-0.05 0.75 · 0.5 · 0.5; FINITE-4 0.75 · 0.5 · 0.5 (FINITE-4-novol the same); FID-0.15-novol 0.25 · 0.25 · 0.25; CAGE-0.25 11.75 (global, 0.083 shift). Probe shift for d ≥ 2: 0 in every regime except CAGE.
claims.refuteBy: Recolour blocks at d ≥ 1 along a seam in a longer slab or at n=16. A FID-0.15 seam shift above 1/256 at a probe more than 0.5 block from the recoloured block refutes it.

claims.statement: The render step finish() re-solves λ over each whole cluster. That shifts the rendered surface D uniformly by up to 0.021 block in response to a block change anywhere in the cluster, even where labels and D0 do not change.
claims.numbers: FID-0.15, Dfull shift at the probe for every d from 2 to 10: 0.00155 (add), 0.0094 (remove), 0.021 (recolour); D0 0 and labels 0 at the same points. The render λ goes 0.07076 → 0.08064 / 0.13104 / 0.20492.
claims.refuteBy: Compare Dfull with D0 at probes more than 2 blocks from the change. If Dfull − D0 is not uniform, or is below 1e-4, the claim fails.

claims.statement: Under FREE, influence is global: one block added at one end of a small cluster moves the far end by almost half a block.
claims.numbers: 1x1x6 A bar, n=16. The base ends as a rounded blob (far-end ray 1.179, side rays 1.062), not a perfect sphere. Shifts along rays from the base centroid, far end / sides: add −0.437 / −0.017; remove +0.441 / −0.152; recolour (end block to B) −0.375 / −0.082.
claims.refuteBy: Re-run with maxSteps 1000 and a longer bar. A far-end shift below 1/64 would refute global influence.

claims.statement: λ tracks surface/volume only loosely. Under FID-0.15 a linear fit with an offset explains 82 % of the variance, but λ ∝ S/V fails. λ depends on cross-section and feature class: 1×1 bars have the same λ at every length, and one inclusion fixes λ_A and λ_B regardless of host size. FREE follows the sphere law λ ≈ 0.2537·V^(−1/3) only where the cluster actually becomes a sphere.
claims.numbers: FID-0.15 over 16 clusters: λ = 0.1076 + 0.0282·S/V, R² 0.817, max residual 0.032; proportional fit max residual 0.091; λ ranges 0.154–0.305. Bars 1x1xL for L = 2, 4, 8: 0.23879 / 0.23917 / 0.23917. At S/V = 3: cube 2³ 0.19297 vs plate 4x1x4 0.1601. Inclusion λ_A 0.20705, λ_B 0.34672 in slabs 3, 5, 7 and a 3x2x9 bar. R² for the other regimes: FID-0.05 0.151, FINITE-4 0.506, CAGE 0.739, FREE 0.779. FREE: cube 2³ 0.12788 vs 0.1268 predicted, bar 1x1x2 0.20039 vs 0.2014; V=4 off by 4–6 %; bar 1x1x8 off by 27 % and cube 3³ by 63 % (pinned before becoming spheres).
claims.refuteBy: Build clusters at fixed S/V with different cross-sections. Equal λ (within 0.005) would refute the cross-section dependence; a change of λ with length for 1×1 bars would also refute it.

claims.statement: Under FID-0.15, convex features are context-free. A convex edge's rounding, a one-block inclusion and the top of a bump take the same shape in every cluster tested; the remaining differences are one-layer terraces. Pits are the exception: depth depends on the smallest host.
claims.numbers: Edge: the top surface has dropped 0.05 at 0.15 block from the edge and 0.25 at 0.025, for slab widths k = 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, a long slab, a hook and a 3³ cube (n=16: 0.125 / 0.025); profile difference from the k=8 reference ≤ 1e-5 beyond the terrace region. Inclusion: top 2.2325 (bulges 0.23) and profile difference 0 in slabs 3, 5, 7 and a bar. Bump top 2.995–2.997 in all hosts; profiles differ by ≤ 0.083 (one terrace). Pit centre: 1.836 in the 3x2x3 slab vs 1.917 in 5x2x5, 7x2x7, the bar and slab 5 with a far bump.
claims.refuteBy: Embed the same edge or inclusion in a new shape (a ring, a long L, a 3-thick slab). A D0 difference above 1/64 within 0.5 block of the feature that is not a whole-layer terrace refutes it.

claims.statement: Thin attached features depend on the whole cluster through λ: a pillar thins, or drains completely, into the plate it stands on as the plate grows. Removing the pressure is worse: under FID-0.15 with volume:false, mean-curvature flow deletes thin features entirely.
claims.numbers: 1x1x3 pillar, width at mid-height (D0). CAGE-0.25: alone 1.496; on plates 3/5/7: 1.056 / 0.688 / 0.488. FID-0.05: alone 1.152; on any plate 0 (drained, the top falls to 2.08–2.33). FID-0.15: alone 1.128; on plates 0.992. FID-0.15-novol: pillar and plates vanish (12→0, 28→0; 52→4.56 at 300 steps); also a 1x2x4 bar 8→0 and one-block inclusions erased.
claims.refuteBy: Repeat at n=16. A CAGE pillar width that does not fall with plate size, or a FID-0.15-novol pillar that survives, refutes it.

claims.statement: In the anchored regimes a straight seam does not move: labels are flat across it. The visible groove is the renderer's Gaussian blur of the unmoved blocks. It is universal, with depth g(x) = σ·Φ⁻¹(1/(1+Φ(|x|/σ))) for σ = renderS = 0.125 block. Under CAGE-0.25 the labels do form a groove: a one-sub-cell notch, identical in every embedding at least 3 blocks wide.
claims.numbers: The discrete blur of unmoved blocks matches the measured D0 groove to 4.75e-6 block. Continuous g matches to ≤ 0.0014 for |x| ≥ 0.04 (0.0538 at x=0, where grid sampling flattens the bottom to 0.0352). Measured groove (n=12): 0.0352 for |x| ≤ 0.04, 0.0243 at 0.08, 0.0143 at 0.12, 0.0045 at 0.20, under 0.001 beyond 0.28. Groove minimum 1.9648 in all 8 FID-0.15 embeddings with widths ≥ 2 (2|2, 3|3, 5|5, 2|5, 5|2, L8, L6, L-hook); also in FID-0.05 and FID-0.15-novol, and 1.9648–1.9656 in FINITE-4. n=16: labels flat, minimum 1.9598. CAGE: notch 1/12 deep and 0.36 wide; profile difference 0 for 3|3, 5|5, 3|3L6 and 2|2L8.
claims.refuteBy: Run FID-0.15 on a straight seam at n=24, or with k between 0.05 and 0.15. A label groove deeper than one sub-cell refutes the 'seam does not move' part. A D0 profile that differs from the discrete blur model by more than 1e-4 refutes the formula part.

claims.statement: Where a seam meets a convex edge (the slab's end face), the groove deepens beyond plain edge-plus-seam addition. The effect dies out within 0.5 block in FID-0.15 and FID-0.05, 1.0 in FINITE-4 and 1.0–1.5 in CAGE-0.25.
claims.numbers: 8x2x4 A|B slab, top height at the seam vs its far value 1.9648. FID-0.15, deviation at x = 0.5/0.4/0.3/0.2/0.1 from the end: 0.0002 / 0.0018 / 0.0099 / 0.040 / 0.124. Groove depth below the local edge height: 0.0866 at 0.1 block vs 0.0352 far away. FID-0.05: 0.0014 at 0.5. FINITE-4: 0.001 at 1.0, 0.022 at 0.75. CAGE: 0.0024 at 1.0, 0.046 at 0.75. End-face notch at mid-height 0.036 (FID-0.15).
claims.refuteBy: Measure on a longer slab, at n=16, or where the seam meets a convex corner. A FID-0.15 deviation above 1/256 more than 0.6 block from the edge refutes it.

claims.statement: Two features superpose exactly (the pair's shape equals the sum of the single-feature changes) only when λ does not change: under FINITE-4, for inclusions 2 or more blocks apart. Under FID-0.15, FID-0.05 and CAGE-0.25 superposition fails by about one sub-cell, because λ shifts.
claims.numbers: B inclusions at x=4 and 4+s in a 14x2x5 A slab, residual (D0) within 1.5 blocks. FINITE-4: s = 2, 3, 4, 6 → ≤ 2.1e-8 with 0 label cells; s = 1 (the inclusions unite) → 0.117. FID-0.15: 0.0926 for s = 2–6 (0.23 at s = 1). FID-0.05: 0.093–0.116 (0.188 at s = 1). CAGE-0.25: 0.098–0.175.
claims.refuteBy: Repeat with bumps, pits, or inclusions next to a seam. A FINITE-4 pair 2 or more blocks apart with a residual above 1/256 refutes it.

claims.statement: Bridging two same-material clusters with one block changes λ for the whole union and re-places its terraces. Near the bridge, labels change within 1.5 blocks. A different-material bridge leaves the two seams on the block faces.
claims.numbers: FID-0.15, two 3x2x5 slabs: λ 0.17529 → 0.08687 (A bridge); 3x2x5 + 6x2x5: 0.17529 / 0.15919 → 0.08983. Label cells within 1.5 blocks 4908, beyond 2340 (one-sub-cell terraces up to 6.3 blocks away). D0 shift up to 0.23 next to the bridge. B bridge: seams at x = 3.0009 and 3.9991; λ_A 0.17295, λ_B 0.19123. The volume:false control changes nothing beyond 0.475 block.
claims.refuteBy: A volume:true bridge with no label change beyond 1.5 blocks, or a volume:false bridge with far changes, refutes it.

claims.statement: At an ambiguous checkerboard X, the smaller pair unites. This holds in FINITE-4, CAGE-0.25 and FREE, and in FID-0.05 when the size ratio is large. With equal sizes, jitter 0 and the reversed block order both give no union, so there is no tie-break bias; jitter alone then decides. FID-0.15 never resolves an X. The painted diagonal line (the thin pair) unites in every regime except FID-0.15.
claims.numbers: 2x2 checker with each pair grown to clusters of 1, 2 or 4 blocks; n=16; variants jitter 0, jitter 1e-3 seeds 1–3, reversed order. Smaller pair unites in all asymmetric cases: FINITE-4 6/6, CAGE 6/6, FREE 6/6 (A1-B4 on 3 variants only). FID-0.05: 4/6 (none at 2v4 and 4v2). FID-0.15: 0/6, and none in all 9 sizes × 5 variants. Equal sizes 1v1, 2v2, 4v4 with jitter 0 or reversed: none in every regime. Seeds split, e.g. FREE 1v1: none / A / both / both / none; CAGE 2v2 gives 'both' in all 5 variants (3D crossing). Painted lines (slab-line, a 4x4 line, colours swapped, 2-high) unite in all variants run under FID-0.05, FINITE-4, CAGE and FREE; FID-0.15 leaves 6 separate dots.
claims.refuteBy: A checkerboard where the larger pair unites under FINITE-4 or CAGE with jitter 0 and reversed order, or an equal-size case that unites with jitter 0, refutes it.

claims.statement: Contact type alone decides some cases. Same-material blocks touching along an edge with air in the other two quadrants always unite; blocks touching only at a corner never do, in every regime.
claims.numbers: diag-edge, diag-edge-3v3 and diag-edge-3v1: A unites in 5/5 variants in all 5 regimes. diag-corner and cube2-cornerA: no union in 5/5 variants in all 5 regimes. cube2-edgeA (an edge contact inside B): unites in FID-0.05, FINITE-4, CAGE and FREE, not in FID-0.15.
claims.refuteBy: Any regime and variant where an edge-with-air contact stays separate, or a corner-only contact unites.

claims.statement: A deterministic local rule reproduces the union outcome. At a lattice edge whose four surrounding blocks form an X: if the other diagonal pair is air, the solid pair connects. Otherwise count the two materials in a window 4×4 across the edge and 3 layers along it; the strictly smaller count connects, and a tie connects nothing. Corner-only contacts never connect. On the painted diagonal line the rule connects the line.
claims.numbers: Agreement with physics over 21 configurations (deterministic variants used where seeds split): FINITE-4 21/21; CAGE 20/21 (misses 'both' in 2v2); FREE 19/20 (misses 'both' in the 3D 2x2x2 checker); FID-0.05 19/21 (2v4 and 4v2: physics none); FID-0.15 10/21 (FID-0.15 never connects an X). slab-line: the rule says A connects, matching FID-0.05, FINITE-4, CAGE and FREE. The rule is Kopf–Lischinski's 'sparse pixels' heuristic for pixel art, cited from memory (inference).
claims.refuteBy: Build configurations where the window count and the true cluster sizes disagree, e.g. a thin line attached to a large blob outside the window. If the physics follows cluster size, the window rule fails.

claims.statement: Under FID-0.15, declaring the line's blocks one cluster does not make a painted line continuous: the X junctions stay pinned with zero neck. The regimes that unite the line give it a neck of 0.5–1.0 block at each X, and under CAGE, FINITE-4 and FREE the line wins even when the opposite union is imposed.
claims.numbers: slab-line, A neck at the 5 X junctions at y=0.5. FID-0.15: physics and imposed union both give 6 components, necks [0,0,0,0,0]. CAGE 0.688 at all 5, also with the B halves imposed united. FINITE-4 0.5 at all 5, also with B imposed. FREE [0,1,1,1,0] in all three. FID-0.05 physics [0,0.875,0.875,0.875,0]; with B imposed, A splits into 2 pieces of 3 blocks.
claims.refuteBy: Re-run at n=12 and n=24. A FID-0.15 imposed union that forms a neck above 0.1 block at the X refutes the first part.

claims.statement: In 2D, FID-0.15 on a flat bar never converges: it locks into an exact 2-cycle in which a whole flat-face layer flips on and off. At n=16 nothing moves at all.
claims.numbers: 24x2 and 8x2 bars, n=32: λ alternates 0.08758 / 0.21242 (= 0.15 ∓ 0.06242), volume 47.96 / 49.41 of 48, 1488 label changes every step for 60 steps. FID-0.05 converges with volume 47.836. FID-0.15-novol converges to 47.836. At n=16: 0 changes from step 1.
claims.refuteBy: Run the 24x2 bar at n=32 for 1000 steps. Convergence, or any cycle other than period 2, refutes it.

An 8x2x4 A|B slab where the seam meets the end edges, with its section (labels unmoved, groove from the render blur). One B inclusion in a 6x2x6 slab.

Task 4, n=16, plans at mid-height. Checkerboards with unequal cluster sizes: the small pair unites (FREE seed 1, CAGE-0.25). Equal-size ties (FREE seed 1; the engine reports A united in A1/B1 although the X is still visible at mid-height). FID-0.15: the X stays. Edge contacts with air unite (FID-0.15, CAGE). 2x2x2 3D checker under FID-0.15: no union.

Task 4, painted diagonal line (slab-line, 6x1x6, n=16). FID-0.15 physics, with the A line imposed united, and with the B halves imposed united: 6 dots, neck 0. FID-0.05 physics: the line unites; with B imposed it is cut into 2. FINITE-4 (neck 0.5), CAGE-0.25 (neck 0.69; it wins even with B imposed) and FREE: the line unites. 3D views for FID-0.15, CAGE and FINITE-4.

optimizations.idea: Run the bubble shape pass as a purely local rule with no global λ, so its reach is under 0.5 block and fits inside the mesher's existing 38³ region (apron 3). Pair it with an explicit thin-feature guard (the PLAN §7.4 kind), because without pressure the dynamics delete thin features.
optimizations.gain: No cross-chunk solve. An edit dirties only blocks within about 1 block of it. Far terraces and the renderer offset disappear by construction. Shape matches the novol controls: changes within 0–0.475 block.
optimizations.risks: Measured: FID-0.15 with volume:false erases 1-wide bars, pillars, 1-thick plates and one-block inclusions. Pressure-driven looks (inclusion bulge +0.23, bump fillets) also go. The guard is untested in combination with this rule.

optimizations.idea: Keep pressure, but as one scalar per cluster updated by a reduction (union-find over the cluster, or a table by feature class), not a quantile solve over every cell. Possibly apply it only to clusters smaller than the apron.
optimizations.gain: Removes terrace jumps and the stored-deficit floods (CAGE +0.25, FID-0.05 mounds). An edit updates one number per touched cluster. Small isolated clusters, where pressure shapes the result, fit inside the apron and can be solved exactly.
optimizations.risks: Inference only, not implemented or tested. λ varies 0.15–0.30 under FID-0.15 and is only roughly predicted by S/V (R² 0.82, ±0.03). Clusters that cross chunks need a shared union-find, and thin attached features still drain (L10).

optimizations.idea: Produce straight seams, convex edges and seam–edge corners from closed forms or small per-corner tables instead of simulating. Skip all work on flat faces more than about 0.5 block from a feature.
optimizations.gain: Under FID-0.15 most surface vertices never move: flat faces are pinned, seams keep their labels, and the edge inset is 0.15/0.025 everywhere. The seam groove is one known function, g(x) = σΦ⁻¹(1/(1+Φ(|x|/σ))). Seam–edge junctions need a reach of ≤ 0.5 block (FID-0.15), at most 1.5 (CAGE). This is the same mechanism as the existing bevel table.
optimizations.risks: The FID/FINITE groove is the renderer's blur, i.e. a look choice, not physics. Pits and thin attached features are context-dependent and cannot be tabulated (L9, L10). CAGE and FINITE-4 junctions reach 1–1.5 blocks.

optimizations.idea: Resolve ambiguous checkerboard and edge contacts with the deterministic 'minority connects' rule (4×4 across the edge, 3 layers along it; ties connect nothing; air-X connects; corner-only never), stored per lattice edge like the bevel table. Where the rule connects, emit a neck about 0.5–0.7 block wide.
optimizations.gain: Deterministic, reads within 2 blocks, needs no simulation, and matches the physics in 21/21 cases (FINITE-4) and 19–20 of 20–21 (CAGE, FREE, FID-0.05). It keeps the painted diagonal line continuous, the owner's hard case. Ties are explicit, so jitter or phase-order dependence is avoided.
optimizations.risks: The tested set cannot tell the window count apart from true cluster size. FID-0.15 physics never connects, so under that regime the rule must also move geometry, because declaring a union alone left neck 0. The 3D 'both' outcomes (CAGE 2v2, FREE 3D checker) are not reproduced.

optimizations.idea: Do not copy finish()'s cluster-wide volume re-solve into any mesh or render path; use a local re-blur (D0, λ = 0) instead.
optimizations.gain: Removes a uniform surface offset of up to 0.021 block (≈ 5/256) that depends on blocks anywhere in the cluster, so chunk seams cannot disagree because of it.
optimizations.risks: The local re-blur loses a little volume at rounded edges, at render level only (FID-0.15 slab: 135.46 vs 140 in novol labels; the render-level loss was not separately measured).

optimizations.idea: Where λ is pinned (FINITE-4-like dynamics), cache per-feature corrections and add them, since features 2 or more blocks apart superpose exactly.
optimizations.gain: Shape = base + Σ cached corrections for inclusions 2 or more blocks apart (residual ≤ 2.1e-8 with 0 label cells). Only pairs closer than 2 blocks need joint evaluation.
optimizations.risks: Fails by one sub-cell (0.093) in FID-0.15, FID-0.05 and CAGE, where λ moves. Tested only for inclusions.

openQuestions: Does the far-field terrace amplitude scale as 1/n? Re-running the 14x2x5 bump at n=24 (or on a smaller slab) would separate discretisation from physics. A continuum model predicts a uniform ΔV/area shift (≈ 0.018 block for the CAGE base, inference).
Would a volume solver that splits tied flat-face layers make FID-0.05, FINITE-4 and CAGE-0.25 local, removing the stored deficits (139.24, 138, 136.08 of 140) and their cluster-wide release?

At a weaker anchor (k between 0.05 and 0.15) or higher n, do straight seams form a real 120° Plateau groove in the labels, and is it still local and universal? At n=12 and 16 the FID-0.15 seam does not move at all.

The ambiguity rule's window count and true cluster size agree on every configuration tested. Which does the physics follow when they disagree (a thin line attached to a large blob outside the window)?
Superposition was tested only for B inclusions. Do bumps, pits and features next to seams or edges also superpose under FINITE-4, and at what separation?

For FREE checker A1/B1 with jitter seed 1 the engine reports A united, yet the plan at mid-height still shows the X. Where is the A link in 3D, and do the 'both' outcomes (CAGE 2v2, FREE 3D checker) mean two pairs crossing at different heights?

What cluster-size threshold would let a game drop the volume constraint (purely local dynamics) while keeping thin features (pillars, 1-thick plates) alive, given that FID-0.15 without pressure erases them?

results.summary:
I did not write REPORT.md: this harness refuses report .md files from subagents. This structured result is the report, and every number in it cites a log or JSON in teams/table/ (backed up with rsync).

**Corner classes.** I enumerated the 2x2x2 neighbourhoods of a lattice corner and checked the counts several ways. Brute force, de Bruijn/Burnside and a fixed-point Burnside agree, and so does team prior's independent count:
- With materials as the unit there are 738 classes. 551 of them are surface classes.
- With clusters as the unit there are 225 classes.
- With solid/air only there are 22 classes.
- Only 76 of the 738 classes (52 of the 551 surface classes) obey Plateau's laws.

**Generated terrain is very concentrated.** Over 448 chunks of seed [1,1] there are 384,419 surface corners:
- 32 classes cover 99% and 62 cover 99.9%.
- 88.8% of surface corners have a single material.
- 12.3% are non-Plateau, almost all same-material diagonal contacts. True four-material X edges are 0.031%.

**Tables from simulated classes.** I simulated all tabulated classes in canonical embeddings (FID-0.15 and FINITE-4, n=12). I then compared those tables against full simulations of 51 terrain windows, 5 build windows and the 36 catalogue configurations.
- A table that keeps the per-bubble volume constraint misses terrain by 0.107 block on average (FID). The cause is that straight edges stay pinned in the embedding but round in real terrain.
- Dropping the volume constraint gives 0.059 (FID) and 0.038 (FINITE). A table learned from terrain gives 0.035–0.040 (2-fold cross-validation). The floor is 0.023: the same corner measured in two shifted windows differs by that much.
- The repo's bevel rule scores 0.136 and unmoved block corners 0.208 on the same terrain corners.
- Larger keys do not help. Keys of 32 or 64 blocks cover only 31% or 5% of held-out terrain corners, and with fallback they score the same 0.040.
- No single 2x2x2 table fits both terrain and small isolated objects. On the catalogue the no-volume table scores 0.153 and the volume table 0.067. What the table lacks is the size or pressure of the bubble, not more neighbours.

**Verdict.** A precomputed table is viable for the mesher on cost and coverage. It is 63 KB, adds 0.14 ms per chunk in Node, and can hold all 551 surface classes. For terrain it stands in for the physics to about 0.04–0.06 block mean. It does not stand in for the physics on small objects or on same-material diagonal contacts, which need connectivity beyond the 2x2x2.

**Changes to the shared engine.** I used a copy of lib/mbo.mjs, src/mbo-clamp.mjs, with two marked changes:
- A clamp-to-edge blur at the grid boundary, so a window cut is not a surface. With a margin of at least 1 block it gives the same result as lib.
- A `bbox` option that fixes the grid bounds.

claims.statement: With materials as the unit, the 2x2x2 neighbourhood of a lattice corner has 21,147 labellings up to material renaming. Up to the 48 cube symmetries (air fixed) these form 738 classes. By number of distinct materials: 0:1, 1:21, 2:125, 3:245, 4:223, 5:94, 6:24, 7:4, 8:1. Of these, 551 contain both air and solid (mesher surface corners), 531 contain air and at least 2 materials, and 186 have no air. Solid/air only gives 22 classes. With clusters as the unit (same material but not face-connected inside the 2x2x2 counts as separate bubbles) there are 6,153 structures and 225 classes. By number of clusters: 0:1, 1:13, 2:47, 3:67, 4:59, 5:26, 6:9, 7:2, 8:1. The 8-material class cannot occur in the game, which has 7 solid materials.
claims.numbers: 738 / 551 / 531 / 186 / 22 / 225 classes; three counting methods agree (brute force, de Bruijn power-group Burnside, fixed-point Burnside); team prior's independent count also agrees
claims.refuteBy: An independent enumeration, e.g. Polya with a different encoding, that gives any different class count.

claims.statement: Non-Plateau junctions are the rule among classes but the exception on terrain. 662 of 738 classes (499 of 551 surface classes) contain at least one of: a lattice edge with 4 films around it (650 classes; 435 with 4 distinct phases), more than 4 bubbles at the corner (280 counting materials, 539 counting clusters), or a same-material diagonal-only contact (513). Only 52 surface classes are Plateau-legal. On generated terrain (wide sample, 384,419 surface corners) 12.26% of surface corners are non-Plateau, almost all ambiguous same-material diagonal contacts. Four-distinct-phase X edges are 0.031%, and corners with more than 4 bubbles counting materials are 0. A terrain surface corner has at most 3 materials.
claims.numbers: Terrain wide sample: ambiguous union 10.84% (single-material 5.90%, multi-material 4.94%); X edges with no solid ambiguity 1.42%; more than 4 bubbles counting clusters 0.37%. bench16: non-Plateau 14.8%. Builds: 6.26% non-Plateau (checker class 14 at 4.65%; house 4-distinct X at 1.61%).
claims.refuteBy: Re-sample other seeds or chunks and find 4-distinct-phase X edges or more than 4 materials at a corner well above 0.1% of terrain surface corners.

claims.statement: Terrain surface corners concentrate in very few classes. In 448 chunks (8x8 chunk columns, cy -2..4, seed [1,1]) there are 384,419 surface corners. They fall into 131 classes; 32 classes cover 99% and 62 cover 99.9%. The top 7 classes are all single-material and cover 79.7%: flat 20.1%, concave edge 14.8%, convex edge 10.9%, concave corner 10.9%, two step classes 9.0% and 7.5%, convex corner 6.5%. Single-material corners are 88.8%. bench16 gives 96 classes, with 33 for 99% and 62 for 99.9%. The synthetic builds give 18 classes, with 15 for 99%.
claims.numbers: Surface corners: wide 384,419; bench16 47,554; builds 2,235. Classes covering 99% / 99.9%: 32 / 62 (wide), 33 / 62 (bench16), 15 / 17 (builds).
claims.refuteBy: Count classes on another seed or a larger chunk sample and find that more than about 50 classes are needed for 99%.

claims.statement: A class table built from canonical embeddings that keep the per-bubble volume constraint is biased against real terrain. The embedding (E2c) extrudes each octant block to 2^3 and continues it past the box with a clamp blur. Measured against full simulations of 51 terrain windows, its vertex lies 0.107 block from the measured vertex on average (FID-0.15) and 0.082 (FINITE-4). The reason is that straight edges and corners stay pinned or under-rounded in the embedding but round in terrain. For the convex edge (class 2) the table gives 0.0375 per axis against a terrain mean of 0.136; the convex corner (class 1) 0.176 against 0.272; the concave corner (class 249) -0.176 against -0.264.
claims.numbers: Mean distance from the measured vertex on terrain-random corners (n 2,260), FID / FINITE: volume E2c table 0.107 / 0.082; bevel 0.136 / 0.121; blocks 0.208 / 0.256. All at n=12.
claims.refuteBy: Repeat at n=16 or 20 and find that edges round in E2c with the volume constraint and the bias falls below about 0.05.

claims.statement: The per-bubble volume constraint (pressure) is what makes the canonical table depend on context. The same E2c embedding run with volume:false reproduces terrain closely. On terrain-random corners the mean distance from the measured vertex is 0.059 (FID-0.15) and 0.038 (FINITE-4); on terrain-seam windows it is 0.049 and 0.037. Weighted by count over the 16 most frequent terrain classes, the gap between canonical and terrain-mean vertex falls from 0.097 to 0.039 (FID) and from 0.066 to 0.0145 (FINITE).
claims.numbers: No-volume table on terrain-random: p90 0.120 / 0.073, p99 0.319 / 0.235 (FID / FINITE). Inference, not measured: the bubble pressures in the terrain windows were not recorded, so 'huge terrain bubbles behave as pressure ~ 0' is an interpretation.
claims.refuteBy: Record the lambda of each bubble in the terrain windows. If they are far from 0, or if a no-volume terrain run differs from the volume run by about 0.05 or more, the mechanism is wrong.

claims.statement: No single 2x2x2 table fits all contexts. The missing input is the bubble's size or pressure, not more neighbours. On the shared catalogue (isolated objects of 1 to 75 blocks) both the no-volume table and the terrain-trained table do badly, while the volume E2c table and the 8-blocks-alone embedding do much better. On builds the volume table is best.
claims.numbers: Catalogue, FID / FINITE: no-volume 0.153 / 0.168; terrain K8 0.151 / 0.151; volume E2c 0.067 / 0.070; E1m 0.079 / 0.098. Builds: volume E2c 0.044 / 0.044; no-volume 0.049 / 0.084. Embedding differences: E1m vs E2c tables differ by a frequency-weighted 0.199 / 0.194; E2c vs E3c (box size) by only 0.0013 / 0.012.
claims.refuteBy: Find a single table, for example keyed on K8 alone with any embedding, that scores below 0.07 on terrain, builds and catalogue together.

claims.statement: Larger keys do not pay on terrain. In 2-fold cross-validation by bench chunk over 3,115 terrain corners (FID-0.15), the 2x2x2 class key K8 covers 97.2% of held-out corners with mean error 0.035 (0.040 including corners that fall back to the E2c table). The other keys add no accuracy once a fallback is included: K32 (2x2x2 plus 24 face neighbours) covers 30.6%, K32eq (face neighbours reduced to 3 states) 33.0%, and K64 (4x4x4) 5.0%, and with fallback to K8 then E2c each scores 0.040 to 0.041. The terrain sample holds 49 distinct K8 keys, 1,602 K32 keys and 2,723 K64 keys among 3,115 corners. Under FINITE-4 K8 scores 0.031 on covered corners and 0.036 with fallback, and the larger keys add nothing either.
claims.numbers: Covered-corner error K32 0.033, K64 0.017 (on 155 corners). Twin-window floor 0.023.
claims.refuteBy: Train on many more windows, for example 500, and show that K32 coverage rises above about 80% with error clearly below K8's 0.035.

claims.statement: Material identity barely moves the vertex on terrain except at seams. A solid/air-only key (K8bin, 13 to 17 entries) scores 0.047 in cross-validation against 0.035 for the full K8 (FID). Multi-material edge and corner classes take the vertex of their single-material counterpart. Examples (terrain means, canonical frame): the grass/dirt slope class 97 is [0,-0.139,-0.139] against concave edge class 95 at [0,-0.137,-0.137]; classes 250, 253 and 257 sit at -0.27 to -0.29 per axis against class 249 at -0.264.
claims.numbers: K8bin trained on terrain and applied to builds: 0.064 (100% coverage); K8: 0.055 (84.1% coverage).
claims.refuteBy: Show terrain seam-free multi-material classes whose mean vertex differs from the single-material class with the same solid mask by more than 0.05.

claims.statement: The physics moves seam vertices in the same direction as the repo's bevel seam shift but by a different amount, and adds a groove. For the flat half with one odd block (class 11, the bevel seam case) the terrain-trained vertex in canonical frame is [0.146, 0.070, 0.146] under FID-0.15 and [0.237, 0.140, 0.237] under FINITE-4. That is an in-plane shift toward the odd block of 0.146 / 0.237 per axis (bevel uses 0.25), plus a dip into the solid of 0.07 / 0.14. On terrain seam corners the bevel rule lies further from the measured vertex than unmoved block corners do; the no-volume table is closest.
claims.numbers: Terrain-random seam corners (n 149), FID: bevel 0.240, blocks 0.157, volume table 0.111, no-volume table 0.068, terrain K8 0.039. Under FINITE: bevel 0.226, blocks 0.263, no-volume 0.077. Seam points are grid-limited to about ±0.02.
claims.refuteBy: Measure seams on labels instead of the render field D, at n=16 or more, and find the class-11 in-plane shift outside 0.1–0.25 per axis.

claims.statement: Giving each (corner, material) its own vertex position is not a viable layout. The per-material surface-nets vertices at a seam corner sit far apart, so splitting positions by material would open cracks. The per-material information belongs in where the single shared vertex sits, namely on the seam (triple line). That is what the mesher's shared-position split already assumes. The class table does predict the per-material vertices well.
claims.numbers: Mean separation of per-material vertices: terrain 0.806 block (FID, n 275), catalogue 0.907. E2c table vs measured per-material vertex: 0.041 (terrain FID). Inference, not measured: the claim that the cracks would show is not rendered.
claims.refuteBy: Show a per-material vertex definition that is local to the seam and keeps the vertices within about 0.1 of each other while staying on the surface.

claims.statement: At mesh time, a direct table indexed by the rank of the corner's restricted-growth string costs 63,441 bytes and adds about 0.14 ms per 32^3 chunk. The table has 21,147 entries of 3 int8 offsets in 1/256 block, already transformed so no symmetry runs at mesh time. In Node on this machine, over the 16 bench chunks (2,972 surface corners per chunk on average), reading the 8 blocks only takes 0.425 ms per chunk and rank plus lookup takes 0.562 ms, i.e. +0.137 ms. The complete no-volume table (all 551 surface classes) computed in 107 s (FID) and 51 s (FINITE) at n=12. Of those entries, 7 (FID) and 6 (FINITE) are clamped to the cell boundary; they account for 0.09% of sampled corners. An offset of 0.5 does not fit int8 at 1/256, so offsets clamp at ±0.496.
claims.numbers: A per-material layout would need 56,674 material slots on surface patterns, 170,022 bytes.
claims.refuteBy: Port the lookup into the repo mesher and measure more than about 1 ms per chunk on the bench chunks.

claims.statement: Same-material diagonal contacts carry a disproportionate share of the table's error, because the union decision depends on connectivity outside the 2x2x2. Under FID-0.15, classes 97, 27 and 92 make up 5.6% of terrain corners but 18.8% of the no-volume table's total error. Class 27 (two blocks touching along an edge, the rest air) has mean error 0.80. Uniting same-material bubbles in the embedding ('mat' semantics) does not fix class 97 under FID: it gives -0.027 per axis against a terrain mean of -0.139.
claims.numbers: 'mat' vs 'clu' table entries: mean difference 0.029 over 65 ambiguous classes (FID), frequency-weighted 0.010. Under FINITE-4 classes 92 and 27 have errors 0.241 and 0.386.
claims.refuteBy: Add a union bit computed from connectivity in the mesh apron and show the ambiguous-class error falls to the level of the other classes (about 0.06).

claims.statement: Engine resolution limits. FID-0.15 is fully pinned at n=8: E2c runs show zero label changes for classes 1, 2 and 10, so the vertex comes only from the render blur. n=12 and n=16 move. For FID, E2c tables at n=12 and n=16 differ by a mean of 0.006 over the top 12 classes. FINITE-4 vertices grow with n and have not converged by n=20: the convex corner (class 1) moves 0.133 / 0.204 / 0.243 / 0.261 per axis at n=8 / 12 / 16 / 20, and n=12 vs n=16 tables differ by 0.030 on average (max 0.128). All comparisons here are at a fixed n=12, the largest that fits 9x8x9 terrain windows in the memory limit.
claims.numbers: Convex edge (class 2) under FINITE-4: 0.040 / 0.081 / 0.121 / 0.138 per axis at n=8 / 12 / 16 / 20.
claims.refuteBy: Run the same classes at n=24 or more (on a smaller box) and show that FINITE-4 converges by n=16.

claims.statement: Measurement floor: the same world corner measured in two terrain windows shifted by (2,0,2) gives reference vertices 0.023 apart on average (FID-0.15) and 0.022 (FINITE-4), over 128 corners. Table errors below about 0.02–0.03 cannot be resolved with 9x8x9 clamped windows and a 2-block guard.
claims.refuteBy: Repeat with larger guards or windows; if the twin difference rises well above 0.03, the window floor is underestimated.

On grass staircases the no-volume table follows the rounded sim surface; the volume table keeps sharper corners.

The owner's hard case, a painted 1-wide diagonal brick line in a stone floor, sliced across the line, FINITE-4, n=12: the sim puts a groove at the seams, which the table vertices follow.

optimizations.idea: For terrain, replace physics with a per-corner table: no-volume canonical-embedding offsets for all 551 surface classes, indexed directly by the rank of the corner's restricted-growth string, with offsets pre-transformed (21,147 x 3 int8, 63 KB).
optimizations.gain: Terrain vertices within 0.059 (FID) / 0.038 (FINITE) block mean of the full simulation, against 0.136 / 0.121 for the current bevel rule and 0.208 / 0.256 for blocks. Cost about +0.14 ms per chunk; no simulation at mesh time.
optimizations.risks: Wrong for small isolated objects (catalogue error 0.153 / 0.168) and for ambiguous diagonal unions (T12). FINITE-4 absolute values depend on n (T13). The table must be frozen for golden hashes, so whatever n and regime it is built at becomes permanent.

optimizations.idea: A two-level table: a 22-entry solid/air table for single-material corners, plus a material-aware table only for seam classes.
optimizations.gain: 88.8% of terrain surface corners need only the 22-entry table. In cross-validation K8bin costs only +0.012 mean error over K8 (0.047 vs 0.035).
optimizations.risks: Seam grooves and seam position come only from the seam table. Builds have 25.7% multi-material corners, so they lean on it more.

optimizations.idea: Key the table on K8 plus a bubble-size or pressure bucket (size of the face-connected cluster within the mesh region, saturating), not on a larger neighbourhood.
optimizations.gain: Could close the gap between terrain (no-volume table best) and small objects (volume or E1m table best): catalogue error 0.15 down toward about 0.07. Untested; inference.
optimizations.risks: Needs a flood fill per mesh job; the 38^3 or 52^3 region bounds the size measure; the extra key multiplies table size by the number of buckets.

optimizations.idea: Do not pursue 32- or 64-block keys or hashed window keys.
optimizations.gain: Avoids tables that cover 5–33% of new corners for no gain once a fallback is used.
optimizations.risks: Based on 3,115 corners from 51 windows of one seed; a much larger training set could raise coverage.

optimizations.idea: Resolve same-material diagonal contacts with an explicit union bit, computed from connectivity in the apron, then look up the table.
optimizations.gain: Targets the classes carrying 18.8% of the no-volume table's FID error on 5.6% of corners; non-Plateau corners are 12.3% of terrain surface corners.
optimizations.risks: The 'mat' experiment shows uniting in the embedding alone does not reproduce terrain for class 97 under FID; the bit must select a separately simulated or learned entry.

openQuestions: Is pressure about 0 the right model for huge terrain bubbles? The per-bubble lambda in the terrain windows was not recorded (T5 is partly inference).
Would a size or pressure bucket in the key close the catalogue gap without hurting terrain? (optimization 3, untested)
FINITE-4 vertices have not converged in n by n=20. At what n should a frozen table be built, and how much would entries move?
Seam distances for the data-driven tables were not measured: seam points were not stored per corner, so only the reference-vertex error bounds them.
All geometry is on the render field D (re-blurred labels, which rounds creases by about 0.1 block). Would label-based geometry change the class-11 seam numbers?
'World' clusters use a 12-block apron around each window. Are there same-material bubbles connected only further away that would change the union in ambiguous classes?
Only seed [1,1]: 448 chunks for frequencies, 51 windows (3,115 corners) for simulations. Do other seeds or biomes (beaches, sand) shift the class shares?
Three FID terrain windows (t1a-shift, t11b, t5a) reached 150 steps without converging; their vertices may be slightly off equilibrium.
